before.title: The uniform second-order Taylor remainder of $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}$ on $[0,z_0]$
before.reference: scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08 ("Taylor with bounded second derivative"; constants depend on z_0); audit-expansion-report.md M08 branch
before.design_state: complete elementary argument from the published Lagrange-remainder supplier with an explicit uniform constant
before.statement:
Let $z_0\in[0,1)$ and define $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, the reciprocal of the nonnegative square root, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

(a) $f$ is differentiable on $(-\infty,1)$ with $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and twice differentiable there with $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; in particular $|f''(z)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$.

(b) For every $z\in[0,z_0]$ there is a real $R(z)$ with $$f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z),\qquad |R(z)|\le K(z_0)\,z^2,$$ so $|f(z)-1|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2$ for $z\in[0,z_0]$. Consequently, for every $\eta>0$, $$0\le z\le\frac{\eta}{\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0}\ \Longrightarrow\ |f(z)-1|\le\eta ;$$ the display is the quantitative form of $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$ used by [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

The lemma is a statement of real analysis about the single function $f$; it attaches no physical meaning to $z$ and makes no claim about a Lorentz factor or a physical velocity.
before.strategy:
(a) Write $f(z)=g(1-z)^{-1}$ with $g(y):=y^{1/2}$ for $y>0$, or directly apply the power rule: by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the rational powers of [[def-rational-power]] agree on rational exponents with the real powers differentiated in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], whose second clause gives $(x^{\alpha})'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$; the affine map $z\mapsto 1-z$ has derivative the constant $-1$ (identity and sum rules, [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]), so the chain rule [[thm-chain-rule]] applied to $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}=y^{\alpha}\circ(1-z)$ with $\alpha=-1/2$ gives $f'(z)=-\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}\cdot(-1)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and repeating with $\alpha=-3/2$ gives $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; the identities $(1-z)^{\alpha}(1-z)^{-\alpha}=1$ and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ are [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. For the bound: from $0\le z\le z_0$ we have $0<1-z_0\le1-z$, so $\tfrac12-$monotonicity in the base of [[lem-rational-power-monotone]] with $r=5/2$ gives $(1-z_0)^{5/2}\le(1-z)^{5/2}$ (equality exactly when $z=z_0$, by the strict part otherwise), and [[lem-of-inverse-positive]] gives $(1-z)^{-5/2}\le(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$; multiplying by $\tfrac34$ and reading $|f''|=f''$ (the strict positivity of the power, [[lem-rational-power-laws]] clause 1) gives the claim.

(b) Put $n=1$, $a=0$, $x=z\in[0,z_0]$ in [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]: $f$ has derivatives through order $2$ on the closed interval between $0$ and $z$ with endpoint continuity (indeed it is $C^{\infty}$ on the open neighbourhood $(-\infty,1)$ of that interval), and $|f''(t)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}=:M$ there by (a); hence $|R_{1,0}f(z)|\le M z^2/2!=K(z_0)z^2$ for $R(z):=R_{1,0}f(z)=f(z)-f(0)-f'(0)z=f(z)-1-\tfrac z2$. The final display follows from $|f(z)-1|\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ for $z\le z_0$ and the order arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ with the absolute-value properties of [[lem-of-abs-value]] ([[def-abs-value]]).

before.title: Compact-support variation: the fundamental lemma, integration by parts and differentiation under the integral sign
before.statement: Work in an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model, identifying a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$ with its image in $\mathbb R^4$; all integrals are Riemann (Darboux) integrals. (a) If $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\int_\Omega g\,\psi\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $\psi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $g=0$ on $\Omega$. (b) If $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ and compactly supported and $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$, then for each $a$, $\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=-\int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$, provided $g$ is $C^1$ on $\Omega$ and the products are extended by zero outside $\operatorname{supp}f$. (c) If $F:(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\Subset\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$. The lemma is choice-free and is stated for the exact Riemann integration theory on bounded rectangles; no distribution theory, no $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ hypothesis and no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: For (a), suppose $g(p_0)\ne0$; by continuity choose a closed axis-parallel box $Q\Subset\Omega$ centred at $p_0$ on which $|g|\ge c>0$, and a smooth bump $\psi$ with $\psi=1$ on a sub-box $Q'\Subset Q$ and support in $Q$ ([[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]); then $\int_\Omega g\psi\ge c\int_{Q'}\psi>0$ by monotonicity and the positivity of the integral of a nonnegative continuous function on a nondegenerate box ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), a contradiction. For (b), extend $fg$ by zero, let $R$ be a box containing its support, apply the fundamental theorem in the coordinate $x^a$ on each line and Fubini's theorem for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]) to conclude $\int_{\mathbb R^4}\partial_a(fg)=0$; expand $\partial_a(fg)$ by [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For (c), apply [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] on a rectangle containing $K$ with the continuous partial $\partial_sF$. No choice principle is used.

after.statement: Work in an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model, identifying a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$ with its image in $\mathbb R^4$; all integrals are Riemann (Darboux) integrals. after.strategy:
(a) Suppose g(p) is nonzero. Set sigma=+1 if g(p)>0 and sigma=-1 if g(p)<0. By continuity there is a closed nondegenerate box Q compactly inside Omega on which sigma*g>=a>0. Choose a smaller closed nondegenerate box Qprime in int(Q). Apply [[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]] to Qprime inside int(Q) to obtain a smooth bump rho with 0<=rho<=1, rho=1 on Qprime and support inside int(Q). Its finite-ball construction gives compact support. Use the signed test psi=sigma*rho. Its integral satisfies integral g*psi=integral (sigma*g)*rho >=a*vol(Qprime)>0, contrary to the hypothesis. Both signs of g(p) are thereby covered.
(b) The products fg, f partial_a g, and g partial_a f have compact support inside Omega. Their extensions by zero are respectively C1 and continuous on R4: near every point outside Omega they vanish on a neighbourhood, because supp(f) is a compact subset of Omega. Choose a bounding rectangle with this support in its interior. On each coordinate line the integral of partial_a(fg) is zero by FTC, since fg vanishes at the endpoints. Apply [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] repeatedly to the continuous functions, and expand the product derivative to obtain the displayed integration-by-parts identity.
(c) Extend F and partial_s F by zero outside Omega. Since the common support K is compactly inside Omega, both extensions are continuous on each compact parameter interval times a bounding rectangle, and differentiation in s gives the extended partial_s F. The imported [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] has a one-spatial-variable public interface; apply it four times to the iterated coordinate integrals, using Fubini for continuous functions at each stage. Continuity of each integrated derivative follows from uniform continuity on the compact product and the bound |integral u|<=vol(R)*sup|u|. This proves C1 parameter dependence on each compact subinterval of (-s0,s0), hence everywhere there. The compactly supported integral does not depend on its bounding rectangle by [[lem-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-is-well-defined]]. All choices are finite; no AC or countable choice is used.

before.title: The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta
before.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), and let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be its coordinates, so that a vector is written x = x^0 e_0 + x^1 e_1 + x^2 e_2 + x^3 e_3 and the spatial part is the coordinate column x_vec = (x^1,x^2,x^3) of R^3 with its standard Euclidean structure (def-euclidean-inner-product). For beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1, where |beta| is the Euclidean norm, set gamma(beta) := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) > 1 (def-rational-power, lem-rational-power-laws). The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta is the linear map B(beta): V -> V defined by its action on coordinates: for beta not equal to 0, x'^0 = gamma (x^0 - beta . x),  x' = x + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . x) beta - gamma beta x^0, and for beta = 0, B(0) := identity, where x' denotes the coordinates of B(beta) applied to the vector with coordinates x, and beta . x is the Euclidean scalar product. Equivalently, in the ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) the matrix of B(beta) is B^0_0 = gamma, B^0_i = B^i_0 = -gamma beta_i for i = 1,2,3, and B^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j for i,j = 1,2,3 (with the last expression replaced by delta^i_j for beta = 0; its beta -> 0 limit is (1/2) beta_i beta_j). In the 1+1 case beta = beta e_1 this reads x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - beta x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0). The vector beta is called the boost parameter; it is dimensionless and mathematically independent of any unit convention.
before.strategy: A definition item, well-defined because the displayed formulas assign to every coordinate pair (x^0,x_vec) a pair (x'^0,x'_vec), and by thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis (applied through def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map) there is a unique linear map with that matrix, namely x |-> E o M o E^{-1}. The beta = 0 case is declared separately because the matrix expression ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) is undefined there; the definition must not silently divide by zero, and the extension is not asserted to be continuous (that is a separate computation). This item asserts no Lorentz property: that B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and that B(-beta) is its inverse is the content of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the composition law is the content of lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition; the physical reading of c beta as a relative velocity is stated only on the physics items of this page, not here.

after.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), and let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be its coordinates, so that a vector is written x = x^0 e_0 + x^1 e_1 + x^2 e_2 + x^3 e_3 and the spatial part is the coordinate column x_vec = (x^1,x^2,x^3) of R^3 with its standard Euclidean structure (def-euclidean-inner-product). In the 1+1 case beta = beta e_1 this reads x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - beta x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0). The vector beta is called the boost parameter; it is dimensionless and mathematically independent of any unit convention.
after.strategy: A definition item, well-defined because the displayed formulas assign to every coordinate pair (x^0,x_vec) a pair (x'^0,x'_vec), and by thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis (applied through def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map) there is a unique linear map with that matrix, namely x |-> E o M o E^{-1}. The beta = 0 case is declared separately because the matrix expression ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) is undefined there; the definition must not silently divide by zero, and the stated limit follows from the explicit rationalization below. This item asserts no Lorentz property: that B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and that B(-beta) is its inverse is the content of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the composition law is the content of lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition; the physical reading of c beta as a relative velocity is stated only on the physics items of this page, not here. For the gamma boundary, gamma is positive and gamma^2=1/(1−|beta|^2)>=1, with equality exactly when |beta|=0, so gamma>=1 with precisely the asserted equality case. For beta!=0 the identity gamma^2−1=|beta|^2 gamma^2 yields (gamma−1)/|beta|^2=gamma^2/(gamma+1). Continuity of the positive power in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] makes gamma tend to1 as beta tends to0, hence that coefficient tends to1/2. Multiplication by beta_i beta_j proves the leading correction and full spatial-block limit: |beta_i beta_j|<=|beta|^2, so [gamma^2/(gamma+1)−1/2]beta_i beta_j=o(|beta|^2). Thus B(beta) tends to the separately declared identity without a hidden division by zero. No physical velocity interpretation is added. Real and rational powers are identified by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]. The Euclidean norm convention gives $|\beta_i|^2\le\sum_k\beta_k^2=|\beta|^2$, hence $|\beta_i|\le|\beta|$ and $|\beta_i\beta_j|\le|\beta|^2$. In the norm meaning of $\beta\to0$, $|\beta|\to0$. For $|\beta|^2\le3/4$ one has $1\le\gamma\le2$, so $|\gamma\beta_i|\le2|\beta|\to0$; also $\gamma-1=|\beta|^2\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)\to0$. Together with the already proved spatial-block limit these are every matrix entry of $B(\beta)\to I$.

before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $m>0$.

(a) For $w\in S$ define the *Newtonian comparison momentum* and the *Newtonian comparison kinetic energy* of the pair $(m,w)$ by $$N_p(m,w):=mw,\qquad N_K(m,w):=\tfrac12\,m\,|w|^2,$$ where $mw$ is the scalar multiple of $w$ by the real number $m$ ([[def-linear-map]]) and $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ ([[def-integer-power]]). With the SI conventions these carry the units kilogram metre per second and joule respectively.

(b) Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]) and let $y:I\to A$ have inertial coordinate path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$; writing $r(t)=r^1(t)e_1+r^2(t)e_2+r^3(t)e_3$ with real functions $r^1,r^2,r^3$, define the *coordinate velocity* $w(t)\in S$ of the path by $$w(t):=(r^1)'(t)\,e_1+(r^2)'(t)\,e_2+(r^3)'(t)\,e_3,$$ the componentwise derivative of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. The comparison functionals along the path are $t\mapsto N_p(m,w(t))$ and $t\mapsto N_K(m,w(t))$.

(c) The functionals $N_p$ and $N_K$ are comparison expressions built from a named inertial frame, the mass parameter $m$ and the path's coordinate velocity. They are not defined by, and do not presuppose, a separately developed Newtonian theory, and this definition asserts no approximation, correspondence, error bound or physical claim; those are the content of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]].
before.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: clause (a) applies the scalar multiple of a vector of the real vector space $V$ (restricted to $S\subseteq V$) and the square of the norm $|\cdot|$ supplied by the frame's spatial structure, both total on $S$; clause (b) uses the componentwise derivative of a function $I\to\mathbb R^3$ and the unique expansion of a vector of $S$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. No division occurs and no choice is used. The definition deliberately introduces no physical correspondence: it only names the two expressions that [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] compares with the model's measured quantities, and the units are the ones fixed by [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

before.title: Galilean limiting chart maps and bounded chart regions
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains")
before.design_state: definition of the family of affine chart maps whose bounded-region limit is proved in lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(b) *Galilean boost.* For $v\in S$ define the affine map $G_v:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $G_v(t,x):=(t,\,x-tv)$.

(c) *Bounded chart region.* For reals $T,R>0$ put $D_{T,R}:=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S:|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, with $|\cdot|$ the norm of the named frame.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.
before.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: for $v\ne0$, $C>|v|$ the number $\gamma_C(v)$ is a rational power of the positive base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ ([[def-rational-power]]), and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$ using the bilinear form $\delta$ and scalar multiplication in $S$; for $v=0$ the middle term is $0/0$ and the map is declared separately to be the identity (the same convention as [[def-lorentz-boost]]). The identification at $C=c$ is a substitution, not a claim: writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$, that is $x'^0/c=\gamma_C(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/C^2)$ and the displayed spatial formula, because $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/C$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/C^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/C)(ct)=vt$. No Lorentz property, no limit and no physical interpretation is asserted; those are the contents of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

before.title: Uniform Galilean limit of the boost charts on bounded regions, and its failure on unbounded regions
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row (Carroll slow-motion discussion pp. 105-106)
before.design_state: complete explicit bound-and-limit argument on the bounded chart region from the pair's own definitions and the uniform Taylor remainder
before.statement:
Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.
before.strategy:
(a) Substitute the definition: $t'-t=\gamma_Ct-\gamma_C\delta(v,x)/C^2-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\delta(v,x)/C^2$; and $x'-(x-tv)=\tfrac{\gamma_C-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)v-\gamma_Ctv+tv=(\gamma_C-1)\bigl(\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{|v|^2}v-tv\bigr)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv)$, using $\gamma_C-1=(\gamma_C-1)$. The case $v=0$ is the separate definition.

(b) Take absolute values in (a) and use the triangle inequality ([[lem-of-triangle-inequality]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]): $|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)|t|+\gamma_C|\delta(v,x)|/C^2$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)|x_\parallel-tv|$. Writing $v=\sum v^ie_i$, $x=\sum x^ie_i$ in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]] gives $\delta(v,x)=\sum_i v^ix^i$, so [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]] yields $|\delta(v,x)|\le|v|\,|x|$, and $|x_\parallel|=|\delta(v,x)|/|v|\le|x|$, hence $|x_\parallel-tv|\le|x|+t|v|$ by the triangle inequality; with $|t|\le T$, $|x|\le R$ this gives the two displays.

(c) Put $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, so $\gamma_C=f(z)$ with $f$ of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]] ([[def-rational-power]]); that lemma gives $|\gamma_C-1|\le z\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)$ for every $z_0\in(0,1)$ with $z\le z_0$ and the quantitative convergence $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$, choose $z_1\in(0,1)$ so small that $|\gamma_C-1|\le\tfrac12$ whenever $z\le z_1$ (so $\gamma_C\le\tfrac32$) and $|\gamma_C-1|\bigl(T+R+|v|T\bigr)\le\tfrac\varepsilon2$; such $z_1$ exists by the display of the Taylor lemma. Now if $C\ge\max\{|v|,|v|/z_1\}$ then $z=|v|^2/C^2\le|v|/C\le z_1$ (because $|v|/C\le1$), and with $C^2\ge 2\cdot\tfrac32|v|R/\varepsilon=\tfrac{3|v|R}{\varepsilon}$ we also get $\gamma_C|v|R/C^2\le\tfrac32|v|R/C^2\le\tfrac\varepsilon2$. Hence both bounds of (b) are at most $\varepsilon$ for every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$: this is $C_\varepsilon:=\max\{|v|,|v|/z_1,\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}$ (with the harmless convention $z_1$ chosen first). Uniformity in $(t,x)$ is exactly the supremum over $D_{T,R}$, and pointwise convergence follows from containment of each point in a bounded region.

(d) For the family $(t,x_\lambda):=(0,\lambda v/|v|)$ with $\lambda>0$ we have, by (a), $x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)\lambda v/|v|$, whose $\delta$-norm is $(\gamma_C-1)\lambda\to\infty$ as $\lambda\to\infty$ (since $\gamma_C>1$ for $v\ne0$); and for $(t,x)=(0,-\mu v)$ with $\mu>0$ we get $t'-t=\gamma_C\delta(v,\mu v)/C^2=\gamma_C\mu|v|^2/C^2\to\infty$ as $\mu\to\infty$. So both suprema are infinite.

after.design_state: complete explicit bound-and-limit argument on the bounded chart region from the pair's own definitions and the uniform Taylor remainder
after.statement:
Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Quantitative rate and uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* Fix $z_0\in(0,1)$ and set $K_0=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, $A_0=\tfrac12+K_0z_0$ and $\Gamma_0=(1-z_0)^{-1/2}$. Whenever $v\ne0$ and $C\ge |v|/\sqrt{z_0}$, the following hold uniformly on $D_{T,R}$: $$|t'-t|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2T+\Gamma_0|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2(R+|v|T)}{C^2}.$$ Thus the rate is $O(C^{-2})$ with explicit constants for fixed $v,T,R,z_0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ For $v\ne0$, put $H=T+R+|v|T$, choose any $z_1$ with $0<z_1\le\min\{z_0,(2A_0)^{-1},\varepsilon/(2A_0H)\}$ (for example the displayed minimum), and set $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{|v|/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}.$$ This is sufficient, and since $z_1<1$ it gives $C_\varepsilon>|v|$. For $v=0$ both errors vanish identically and any $C_\varepsilon>0$ suffices. Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.
after.strategy:
(a) Subtract the Galilean values from the definition: t'-t=(gamma_C-1)t-gamma_C delta(v,x)/C^2 and x'-(x-tv)=(gamma_C-1)(x_parallel-tv). For v=0 both maps are the identity and both differences vanish.

(b) Scalar absolute-value triangle inequality gives |t'-t|<=(gamma_C-1)|t|+gamma_C|delta(v,x)|/C^2. In a delta-orthonormal basis, thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite gives |delta(v,x)|<=|v||x|. The spatial inner-product norm's homogeneity and triangle inequality are cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm: |x_parallel|=|delta(v,x)|/|v|<=|x|, hence |x_parallel-tv|<=|x_parallel|+|-tv|<=|x|+|t||v|. The absolute value of t is essential for negative chart times. Since gamma_C>=1, |t|<=T and |x|<=R, substitution proves both bounded-region displays.

(c) Fix z0 in (0,1). For 0<=z=|v|^2/C^2<=z0, the Taylor supplier's first remainder bound gives 0<=gamma_C-1<=z/2+K0 z^2<=A0 z. Positive-base rational-power monotonicity and reciprocal order give gamma_C<=(1-z0)^(-1/2)=Gamma0. Substitute into (b) to obtain both explicit C^-2 bounds. For epsilon>0, set H=T+R+|v|T>0 and choose 0<z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)}; each entry of the minimum is positive. For C>=|v|/sqrt(z1), z<=z1, so gamma_C-1<=A0 z1<=1/2 and (gamma_C-1)H<=epsilon/2. Thus gamma_C<=3/2. If also C>=sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon), the additional time term gamma_C|v|R/C^2<=epsilon/2, so both error bounds from (b) are <=epsilon on the whole bounded region. Because z1<=z0<1 and |v|>0, the first threshold is strictly larger than |v|; the inadmissible boost boundary C=|v| is excluded. For v=0 handle the identity family separately with any positive threshold. Supremum over the bounded region gives uniform convergence; each fixed point lies in such a region, giving pointwise convergence.

(d) For v nonzero and fixed C>|v|, gamma_C>1. At (t,x)=(0,lambda v/|v|), lambda>0, the spatial error norm is (gamma_C-1)lambda, unbounded as lambda increases. At (t,x)=(0,-mu v), mu>0, the time error is gamma_C mu |v|^2/C^2, unbounded as mu increases. Thus both whole-domain suprema are infinite. This is a coordinate-family limit only; it changes no physical postulate, adopted constant c, trajectory, force or interaction. No omitted expression or qualitative smallness choice replaces a quantitative step.

before.statement:
Take $v=e_1$ (so $|v|=1$), $T=1$, $R=2$ and the point $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)$ in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]], and let $\Phi_{v,C}(1,2e_1)=(t',x')$. Then for $C=10$: $\gamma_C=(99/100)^{-1/2}=10/\sqrt{99}=10/(3\sqrt{11})\approx1.0050378153$, $t'\approx0.9849370590$, $x'\approx1.0050378153$, so with the Galilean value $G_v(1,2e_1)=(1,e_1)$,
$$|t'-t|\approx0.0150629410\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\tfrac{|v|R}{C^2}\approx0.0251385716,$$ $$|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0050378153\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T)\approx0.0151134458 ;$$ for $C=100$ the same quantities are $\gamma_C\approx1.0000500038$, $|t'-t|\approx0.0001500063\le0.0002500138$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0000500038\le0.0001500113$. The observed deviations shrink by the factors $\approx100.4$ and $\approx100.7$ when $C$ grows from $10$ to $100$, consistent with the $O(1/C^2)$ rate of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(b). Finally, for the tolerance $\varepsilon=0.01$ the same lemma's proof requires only $z\le z_1$ with $z_1\approx1/900$ and $C^2\ge3|v|R/\varepsilon=600$; the choice $C=30$ satisfies both and gives $|t'-t|\approx0.0016674389$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0005560189$, both below $0.01$. All decimals are rounded values of the exact expressions; the example asserts no physical interpretation of the family $\Phi_{v,C}$.
before.strategy: Substitute the data into the definition: $\delta(v,x)=\delta(e_1,2e_1)=2$ and $|v|=1$, so $\gamma_C=(1-1/C^2)^{-1/2}$, $t'=\gamma_C(1-2/C^2)$ and $x'=2+2(\gamma_C-1)-\gamma_C$ by [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]; the displayed values are the evaluations at $C=10$ and $C=100$, with $\gamma_{10}=10/(3\sqrt{11})$ and $\gamma_{100}=(9999/10000)^{-1/2}$ computed through [[lem-rational-power-laws]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]], rounded to ten significant digits. The two bound comparisons are the inequalities of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(b) at $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)\in D_{1,2}$; the ratio check is the quotient of the rounded deviations. The $\varepsilon=0.01$ instance is the explicit choice of the lemma's proof with $z_1=1/900$, $|\gamma_C-1|(T+R+|v|T)\le\ldots$ evaluated at $C=30$; every comparison is arithmetic in $\mathbb R$ and no claim about the model's constant $c$ is made, because $C$ is the auxiliary speed scale of the definition.

The ratios of the exact deviations, evaluated before rounding, are approximately 100.4154227043 and 100.7487483984, respectively. Finally, for tolerance $\varepsilon=0.01$, take $z_0=1/4$. Then $K_0=4\sqrt3/9$ and $A_0=1/2+\sqrt3/9<3/4$. Choose exactly $z_1=1/900$. With $H=T+R+|v|T=4$, one has $z_1<z_0$, $A_0z_1<1/1200<1/2$ and $A_0Hz_1<1/300<\varepsilon/2=1/200$, so every threshold inequality is satisfied. The sufficient threshold is $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{1/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}=\max\{30,\sqrt{600}\}=30>1=|v|.$$ Thus $C=30$ is sufficient uniformly on $D_{1,2}$. At the specified point $\gamma_{30}=30/\sqrt{899}$, $|t'-t|=1-449/(15\sqrt{899})\approx0.0016674389$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|=30/\sqrt{899}-1\approx0.0005560189$, both below $0.01$. The whole-region bound values at $C=30$ are approximately $0.0027794768$ and $0.0016680568$, also below $0.01$. after.strategy: With delta(e1,2e1)=2 and |v|=1, put g_C=C/sqrt(C^2-1). The definition gives gamma_C=g_C, t'=(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and x'=g_C e1; the Galilean value is (1,e1). At C=10,30,100, t'<1: both sides are positive, and (C^2-2)^2<C^2(C^2-1) is equivalent to 4<3C^2. Thus the exact deviations are d_t(C)=1-(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and d_x(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1. The exact uniform bound values from lemma(b) are B_t(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1+2/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and B_x(C)=3(C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1). Evaluate these exact radical expressions at the three scales, then round to ten places after the decimal point. Ratios are evaluated from the exact radical expressions, not already rounded deviations: d_t(10)/d_t(100)=100.4154227043 to ten decimal places and d_x(10)/d_x(100)=100.7487483984 to ten decimal places, hence 100.4 and 100.7 to one decimal place. For the tolerance proof, z0=1/4 gives K0=(3/8)(3/4)^(-5/2)=4sqrt(3)/9 and A0=1/2+sqrt(3)/9<3/4, since sqrt(3)<9/4 follows by squaring the positive quantities: 3<81/16. Therefore z1=1/900 is positive, <=z0, A0 z1<1/1200<1/2 and A0 H z1<1/300<1/200=epsilon/2. This proves z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)} explicitly. The sufficient threshold is |v|/sqrt(z1)=30, while sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon)=sqrt(600)<30 because 600<900; hence C_epsilon=30>|v|. The lemma therefore controls both errors uniformly on the entire bounded region. Exact radical evaluation gives the stated point and bound values at C=30. No ellipsis or empirical claim is used, and the fixed model scale c is not varied.

before.title: First variation of the scalar-field action and the Euler-Lagrange equation
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $K>0$ (joule per metre), let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth (values in inverse square metres) and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Expand the first variation: the derivative term is $-\frac{K}{c}\int\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh$; integrate by parts in the coordinate $x^b$ using [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(b) to move $\partial_b$ onto $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi$, and use $\eta^{ab}\partial_b\partial_a\varphi=\Box\varphi$ (relabeling and [[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]). This proves (a). For (b), if $\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ then $\delta S=0$; conversely, the continuous function $g:=\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)$ satisfies $\int g h=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $h$, so $g=0$ by [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a). Sources: the displayed action and its variation are the flat restriction of (4.42)-(4.43) of the cited Tong text; the argument is standard. No choice principle is used.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos (Michaelmas Term 2019); c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t; 4.5.1-4.5.5 printed pp. 181-191: scalar-field action (4.42)-(4.43) and equation of motion, Hilbert energy-momentum tensor (4.46), diffeomorphism invariance and conservation (4.50), flat-space Noether form, scalar tensor (4.51), Maxwell tensor (4.52), perfect fluid (4.53) with conservation equations (4.54)-(4.55), and the flat-space conserved-charge box argument of 4.5.5

after.title: First variation of the scalar-field action and the Euler-Lagrange equation
after.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $K>0$, let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used. Precisely, with $L(\phi):=\tfrac12\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\partial_b\phi+V(\phi)$, define the relative action $S_h(s):=-(K/c)\int_\Omega[L(\varphi+sh)-L(\varphi)]\,d^4x$. Its integrand has support in $\operatorname{supp}h$, so it is defined for every real $s$ even when either background action diverges; $S_h\prime(0)=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$.
after.strategy: For a fixed compactly supported h, the density difference L(phi+sh)-L(phi) and its s-derivative are supported in supp(h). On each bounded parameter interval they are continuous with continuous s-derivative, so [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]], clause (c), differentiates the relative action and gives exactly the stated first variation. Apply clause (b) to h and eta^{ab} partial_a phi, noting the metric components are constant, to obtain delta S=(K/c) integral(Box phi-Vprime(phi))*h. Mixed partial symmetry gives the displayed Box formula. If the residual is zero, stationarity follows. Conversely stationarity against every compactly supported h makes the continuous residual vanish by clause (a), including both signs. Neither a full-domain background action nor a boundary condition is used. This is the compact-support flat specialization of Tong (4.42)-(4.43) and its equation-of-motion calculation, with the relative functional made explicit; no choice principle is used.

before.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J := rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component satisfies J^0 = rho_0 U^0; writing rho := J^0 (the coordinate density in the chart) and u := U/U^0 (the coordinate velocity), one has rho = rho_0 u^0. Coordinate density and the scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: they agree only in charts in which u^0 = 1. after.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
after.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J:=rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component is J^0=rho_0 U^0. Future timelikeness gives U^0>0 in every inertial chart, so define the normalized chart direction u:=U/U^0 and the coordinate density rho:=J^0. Then u^0=1, u^i=U^i/U^0, rho=rho_0 U^0, and J=rho u pointwise. The coordinate density rho and scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: rho=rho_0 if and only if rho_0(U^0−1)=0; at points where rho_0!=0 equality holds exactly when U^0=1. The vector u is a normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity normalization. In an x^0=ct convention the associated spatial coordinate velocity, if interpreted as such, has components c u^i; physical current/density identification requires its own model premise. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.

(i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. (v) An alternating covariant field is a covariant tensor field, so the slot-by-slot covariant law applies; for the volume form, which by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an oriented frame, the transformation multiplies the determinant by det(Lambda^{-1}) = 1, and by det Lambda = -1 in the improper case. (vi) is the matrix multiplication of the boost matrix with the component vector; (vii) A future timelike vector has positive time component in any oriented inertial chart. Thus U^0 is nonzero and u:=U/U^0 is well-defined, with u^0=1 and u^i=U^i/U^0. Componentwise multiplication gives J^0=rho_0 U^0=:rho and J=rho_0 U=rho_0 U^0(U/U^0)=rho u. Therefore rho−rho_0=rho_0(U^0−1), giving precisely the asserted equality cases, including rho_0=0. C^1 regularity of J follows by the componentwise product rule. before.title: The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so Lambda^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting nabla_X Y from each vector argument and adding it to each covector argument; in inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of the component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation.
before.strategy: Definition with well-definedness obligations. (i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the displayed finite computation using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in (b) is the standard derivation rule on the evaluation of a tensor; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. (iv) In (d), the canonical isomorphism T_pA = V is independent of p, so the covariant derivative along a curve coincides with the ordinary derivative and parallel transport is trivial; this is exactly what makes Fermi-Walker transport below an ordinary linear ODE. No choice principle is used.

after.statement:
Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. abla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)=X[T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)]-\sum_iT(\alpha_1,\ldots,
abla_X\alpha_i,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,
abla_XY_j,\ldots,Y_s)$. In inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of that component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation. (e) First-order C1 version. For C1 vector fields X,Y and C1 covector/tensor fields on Omega, the same directional/evaluation definitions are well-defined and have continuous coefficients: in an inertial chart $(
abla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$ and each tensor component is differentiated in the same way. The component recovery and subtraction of all argument derivatives remain valid. C1 scalar multiplication satisfies the same first-order Leibniz rules, metric compatibility remains $
abla\eta=0$, and the first-order torsion identity uses the continuous coordinate bracket $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$. No C1 closure of this bracket or second covariant derivative of arbitrary C1 data is asserted. For C2 vector fields the second derivatives needed for the zero-curvature identity in(c) exist, and that identity follows by equality of the continuous mixed second partials. All original smooth-field properties and the C1 along-curve derivative in(d) are retained.
after.strategy: Definition with well-definedness obligations. (i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the corrected identity X'^b partial'_b Y'^a=Lambda^a_c X^b partial_b Y^c, equivalently inverse-Lambda recovery of the unprimed components, using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in(b) subtracts the derivative of every argument, whether vector or covector. In an inertial chart use the constant coordinate basis and constant dual basis; their covariant derivatives vanish, so evaluating the rule on those bases leaves only X acting on each tensor component. For variable arguments the ordinary product rule cancels all their derivatives with the displayed subtractions. This proves the stated coordinate formula and the evaluation derivation rule; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. No choice principle is used. For(e), a C1 map Y has continuous differential, and differentiating $Y(p+tX(p))$ at zero gives $dY_p[X(p)]$; the continuous product of dY and X yields the claimed C0 field. The coordinate tensor rule is identical on constant bases, with the ordinary C1 product rule for variable arguments. Only first derivatives occur in the C1 Leibniz/metric/torsion assertions. When X,Y,Z are C2, the fields $\nabla_YZ$ and $\nabla_XZ$ are C1, so the two iterated derivatives and the bracket term in the curvature identity are defined; expansion cancels the first-order bracket terms and the remaining mixed second partials commute. This supplies the actual first-order C1 interface used by dust/fluid and the C1 Bell generator with its explicitly given C2 flow family, without treating C1 fields as smooth or promising a joint C2 flow for every C1 field.

before.title: Stress-energy tensor, force density and local balance on flat spacetime
before.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set. (a) A \emph{stress-energy tensor} on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p$, $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so its inertial components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)). (b) In the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] with length coordinates $x^0=ct$, the components $T^{ab}$ have the unit joule per cubic metre; the frame components are read as energy density ($T^{00}$), energy flux and momentum density ($T^{0i}=T^{i0}$) and stress ($T^{ij}$). This clause fixes a unit and a reading convention only; it asserts no measurement, no matter model and no dynamics. (c) The \emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv) the components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. One says that $T$ is \emph{locally conserved}, or \emph{balanced}, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Definition item fixing the class of fields, the component readings and the balance terminology. Obligations: (i) $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ is chart-independent because $T$ is a symmetric bilinear form and the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) is linear in the tensor; (ii) $\partial_aT^{ab}$ is a $(1,0)$-component family under an affine change of inertial chart by clause (iv) of the same theorem, since the transition matrix is constant; (iii) the unit statement is a convention imported from [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] extended to the density components, and carries no mathematical content; (iv) no positivity, symmetry of the integral representation, conservation or dynamics is asserted. No choice principle is used.

No choice principle is used. For a merely continuous tensor ($k=0$), the component conventions and pointwise contractions are defined, while divergence, four-force density and the balance terminology in (c) require the additional $C^1$ hypothesis; no derivative of a merely continuous field is asserted.
after.strategy: Definition of symmetric C^k type-(2,0) fields for k>=0, and of their divergence only for k>=1, with purely numerical component conventions. Symmetry is chart-independent by the rank-two tensor transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], clause (iii). For k>=1, under an affine inertial transition xprime=Lambda x+a the constant inverse Jacobian in partialprime_a cancels the first Lambda factor in Tprime^{ab}; hence partialprime_a Tprime^{ab}=Lambda^b_d partial_c T^{cd}, clause (iv). This proves chart-independence of the divergence field. The constants and component families in (b) are numerical definitions, not assertions of measured energy or momentum. No conservation, positivity, matter model, slice convergence or choice principle is asserted. The C0 case is well-defined by the existing tensor-field supplier, which permits k=0; the rank-two component law and symmetry use finite linear evaluation and no derivative of T. The observer decomposition expands delta=h-n tensor n pointwise, so its original continuous-T scope and all contraction/uniqueness conclusions are retained. The C1 and higher cases keep exactly the original divergence and balance claims.

before.title: A prescribed covariant stress-energy tensor need not be conserved
before.statement: In an inertial chart let $\Omega$ be open and connected and let $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$; define the smooth symmetric field $T^{ab}:=F\,\eta^{ab}$. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=\eta^{ab}\partial_aF=\partial^bF$, so $T$ is conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $F$ is constant, and for nonconstant $F$ the balance is $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial^bF$ with nonzero four-force density. Since $\eta$ is constant in every inertial chart, the tensor expression $F\eta$ transforms covariantly under every affine Lorentz map; hence Lorentz covariance of a prescribed tensor expression does not by itself imply conservation, and the balance of an arbitrary prescribed $T$ is an additional premise rather than a consequence of its tensor character. The field $T=F\eta$ is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models.
before.strategy: Compute $\partial_a(F\eta^{ab})$ using $\partial_a\eta^{ab}=0$ in inertial coordinates; conservation is equivalent to $\partial^bF=0$ for all $b$, i.e. to $F$ constant on the connected domain. The covariance remark follows from [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) with $\eta'=\eta$. No choice principle is used.

after.title: A prescribed covariant stress-energy tensor need not be conserved
after.statement: In an inertial chart let $\Omega$ be nonempty, open and connected and let $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$. The symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T^{ab}=F\eta^{ab}$ is $C^1$, and its continuous force density is $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}=\eta^{ab}\partial_aF=\partial^bF$. It is conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $F$ is constant; if $F$ is nonconstant then $f$ is not identically zero, although it can vanish at some points. For the smooth explicit witness $\Omega=\mathbb R^4$, $F(x)=(x^1)^2$, one has $f=(0,2x^1,0,0)$, which vanishes on the plane $x^1=0$ and is nonzero off it. The tensor expression $F\eta^{-1}$ is covariant under every affine Lorentz change of inertial chart: for $x'=\Lambda x+a$ the scalar component is $F'(x')=F(\Lambda^{-1}(x'-a))$ and $T'^{ab}=F'\eta^{ab}$. Thus covariance of a prescribed tensor expression does not itself imply conservation; balance is an additional premise. The field is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models.
after.strategy: Differentiate $F\eta^{ab}$ with the constant inverse metric to obtain the force formula. Nondegeneracy of the metric makes $f=0$ equivalent to all partial derivatives of $F$ vanishing. A $C^1$ scalar is totally differentiable ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]]), so the exact connected-open zero-derivative theorem ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]) gives constancy; the converse follows directly. For $F=(x^1)^2$ compute $f=(0,2x^1,0,0)$, including its stationary plane. Apply the earlier tensor law ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)) with the scalar pulled back to the same physical point and $\Lambda\eta^{-1}\Lambda^{\mathsf T}=\eta^{-1}$. This proves covariance without deriving conservation. No choice principle is used.

before.title: A static uniaxial stress: tension must be constant along the stressed direction
before.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). Then the balance components are $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_1T^{10}=0$ and $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, so $T$ is conserved on a connected chart domain if and only if $P$ is constant there; the energy density $\rho(x^1)$ may vary while the tension must be uniform along the stressed direction. This reproduces the static equilibrium condition of a uniform rope under tension and shows that conservation constrains the stress, not the energy density, in this configuration. The example is a component computation and asserts no material model.
before.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}$ directly from the displayed components: the only nonzero derivatives are $\partial_1(\rho e_0\otimes e_0)=0$ and $\partial_1(P e_1\otimes e_1)=P'(x^1)e_1\otimes e_1$; hence conservation is equivalent to $P'=0$. Source: Crowell Example 8 pp. 188-189 (rope under tension; the constant-tension condition), read with the framework's $(-,+,+,+)$ sign conventions. No choice principle is used.

after.title: A static uniaxial stress: tension must be constant along the stressed direction
after.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). Then the balance components are $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0\rho(x^1)=0$ and $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P'(x^1)$, so $T$ is conserved on a connected chart domain if and only if $P$ is constant there; the energy density $\rho(x^1)$ may vary while the tension must be uniform along the stressed direction. This reproduces the static equilibrium condition of a uniform rope under tension and shows that conservation constrains the stress, not the energy density, in this configuration. The example is a component computation and asserts no material model.
after.strategy: The components are $T^{00}=\rho(x^1)$, $T^{11}=P(x^1)$ and all others zero. Thus $\partial_aT^{a0}=\partial_0T^{00}=0$, $\partial_aT^{a1}=\partial_1T^{11}=P\prime(x^1)$, and the $b=2,3$ components vanish. In general the full tensor derivative $\partial_1(\rho e_0\otimes e_0)=\rho\prime e_0\otimes e_0$ is nonzero; it does not enter the divergence because its first tensor index is $0$. Therefore conservation is equivalent to $P\prime=0$ on the interval of $x^1$ values attained in the chart. The $x^1$ range of a connected chart domain is an interval: if an intermediate value $r$ were absent, the nonempty relatively open sets $\Omega\cap\{x^1<r\}$ and $\Omega\cap\{x^1>r\}$ would disconnect the domain. Thus on this interval and [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] makes $P$ constant there. The density profile remains unrestricted apart from its stated $C^1$ regularity. Source: Crowell Example 8 pp. 188-189 with the stated signature conversion; no material model or force law is deduced. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action on flat spacetime
before.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with inertial chart $x$, $K>0$ (joule per metre), $V:\mathbb R	o\mathbb R$ smooth and $\varphi:\Omega	o\mathbb R$ smooth ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]). Let $h$ be a smooth symmetric $(0,2)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ with compact support, and for $|s|<s_0$ small enough that $g_{\mu
u}(s):=\eta_{\mu
u}+s\,h_{\mu
u}$ is nondegenerate with negative determinant on $\operatorname{supp}h$ (such $s_0>0$ exists) set $$\mathcal A(s):=- rac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(	frac12 g^{ab}(s)\,\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi+V(\varphi)\Big)\sqrt{-\det g(s)}\,d^4x .$$ (a) $\mathcal A$ is differentiable at $0$ and $$ rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)=+ rac{1}{2c}\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x,\qquad T^{ab}:=K\Big(\partial^a\varphi\,\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab} ig(	frac12\partial_c\varphi\,\partial^c\varphi+V(\varphi) ig)\Big),$$ where indices are moved with $\eta$. (b) $T$ is the unique continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ whose pairing against every compactly supported smooth symmetric variation $h$ equals $+(2c) rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)$, i.e. $\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x=2c\, rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)$; it is symmetric and its components have the unit joule per cubic metre. It is called the \emph{Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action}. (c) The definition uses only compactly supported metric variations; no boundary terms, no global invertibility of $g(s)$ outside the support of $h$, and no boundary conditions at infinity are used. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Differentiate under the integral sign ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)): the $s$-derivative of the integrand at $0$ is $\tfrac12(\delta g^{ab})\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi+(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V)\delta\sqrt{-\det g}$ with $\delta g^{ab}=-h^{ab}$; the determinant variation $\delta\sqrt{-\det g}=+\tfrac12\eta^{ab}h_{ab}$ at $g=\eta$ is the adjugate/cofactor first-order expansion of the determinant ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]], [[thm-leibniz-determinant-is-alternating-multilinear-and-normalized]], [[cor-determinant-of-an-inverse]]), the variation of the inverse metric is $\delta g^{ab}=-h^{ab}$, and collecting terms gives $d\mathcal A/ds(0)=\frac{K}{2c}\int[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial\varphi^2+V)]h_{ab}\,d^4x$, which is the displayed $T$ paired with $h$. Uniqueness of $T$ follows from [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a) applied componentwise to the continuous difference of two candidates. Sources: the Hilbert definition is (4.46) of Tong and (4.51) for the scalar branch; the flat restriction removes the $\sqrt{-g}$ factor at $g=\eta$ in the final formula but not in the variation. No choice principle is used.

after.title: The Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action on flat spacetime
after.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be any nonempty open set with inertial chart $x$, let $c,K>0$ be numerical constants, and let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For each smooth symmetric $(0,2)$ tensor $h$ with compact support, set $g_{ab}(s)=\eta_{ab}+s h_{ab}$. Choose $s_0>0$ so that these matrices are nondegenerate with negative determinant for $|s|<s_0$; outside $\operatorname{supp}h$ they equal $\eta$. Put $D_h(s,x):=[\tfrac12 g^{ab}(s,x)\partial_a\varphi(x)\partial_b\varphi(x)+V(\varphi(x))]\sqrt{-\det g(s,x)}$ and define the relative action $$\mathcal A_h(s):=-\frac Kc\int_\Omega[D_h(s,x)-D_h(0,x)]\,d^4x.$$ This is the integral of a compactly supported density difference, without assuming either background density has a finite integral. (a) $\mathcal A_h$ is differentiable at $0$ and $$\mathcal A_h\prime(0)=\frac1{2c}\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x,\qquad T^{ab}:=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))],$$ with indices raised by $\eta$. (b) $T$ is smooth and symmetric, and is the unique continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ field for which $\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x=2c\mathcal A_h\prime(0)$ for every such $h$. It is called the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of this scalar-field density. (c) The result holds on unrestricted open $\Omega$, uses only compactly supported metric variations, and imposes no convergence or boundary condition at infinity. If the full background action happens to exist, the relative action is its variation difference and gives the same derivative. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy:
On the compact support of h its entries are bounded. The determinant is a polynomial in s with continuous coefficients, and det(eta)=-1; compactness supplies a uniform s0 for which det(g)<0. The adjugate formula then makes the inverse entries smooth in s and x, as is the square root. Outside supp(h), g=eta. Thus D_h(s)-D_h(0) and its parameter derivative have a common compact support; the compact-variation lemma applies to the relative integral.
Differentiate g^{ac}g_cb=delta^a_b to obtain delta g^{ab}=-eta^{ac}eta^{bd}h_cd=-h^{ab}. Cofactor expansion gives delta det(g)=det(eta)*eta^{ab}h_ab=-eta^{ab}h_ab, so delta sqrt(-det(g))=+(1/2)eta^{ab}h_ab. Therefore delta D=-(1/2)h^{ab}partial_a phi partial_b phi+(1/2)eta^{ab}h_ab L(phi). Multiplication by -K/c gives exactly +(1/(2c))integral T^{ab}h_ab. Symmetry and smoothness follow from the formula. For uniqueness, take a continuous symmetric difference Q: a test with one diagonal component psi gives integral Q^{aa}psi=0; a test with h_ab=h_ba=psi for a<b gives 2 integral Q^{ab}psi=0. The signed fundamental lemma yields every component Q^{ab}=0. Tong (4.46) uses the inverse-metric variation convention; converting it to the covariant variation delta g_ab=h_ab yields the positive sign here. This convention change, compact density difference, and explicit finite-dimensional derivation preserve the source-derived formula without presuming a convergent background action. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Stress balance and finite flux on closed boxes
before.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: For (a): for fixed values of the remaining coordinates, $x^a\mapsto T^{ab}$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$, so one-variable FTC ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}\,dx^a=T^{ab}(d_a)-T^{ab}(c_a)$; integrate this identity over the remaining three coordinates and sum over $a$, using Fubini/iterated integration for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]]) and integrability of continuous functions on boxes ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). For (b): apply (a) to the sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and identify the first and last faces with $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ and the spatial faces with the displayed side-flux terms; continuity of $Q^b$ follows from continuity of $T^{0b}$ and the integral estimate ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). (c) is immediate from (b). Source: this is the flat finite-box flux argument of S9 of the research supplier argument, the restricted version of Crowell 9.3.2-9.3.3 pp. 192-195, with the arbitrary-region argument declined. No choice principle is used.

after.strategy: For (a): for fixed values of the remaining coordinates, $x^a\mapsto T^{ab}$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$, so one-variable FTC ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}\,dx^a=T^{ab}(d_a)-T^{ab}(c_a)$; integrate this identity over the remaining three coordinates and sum over $a$, using Fubini/iterated integration for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]]) and integrability of continuous functions on boxes ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). For (b): apply (a) to the sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and identify the first and last faces with $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ and the spatial faces with the displayed side-flux terms; continuity of $Q^b$ follows quantitatively: the continuous $\partial_0T^{0b}$ is bounded by some $M$ on the box because continuous rectangle integrability includes boundedness ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]); FTC and the integral bound give $|Q^b(s)-Q^b(r)|\le\operatorname{Vol}(K)M|s-r|$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). (c) is immediate from (b). Source: this is the flat finite-box flux argument of S9 of the research supplier argument, the restricted version of Crowell 9.3.2-9.3.3 pp. 192-195, with the arbitrary-region argument declined. No choice principle is used.
