before.title: Divergence-free stress-energy with a nonconserved slice integral
before.statement: In an inertial chart define the smooth symmetric field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$ in the $(e_0,e_1)$ block and $0$ in all components involving $e_2$ or $e_3$. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ everywhere: $\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1-1=0$ and $\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0$. Nevertheless the slice integral $Q^0(s)=\int_0^LT^{00}(s,x)\,dx=sL$ is not independent of $s$: on the spatial interval $K=[0,L]$ the field has a nonzero side flux $T^{10}(x=L)=-L$ and zero flux at $x=0$, and the exact balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] gives $Q^0(s_2)-Q^0(s_1)=-\int_{s_1}^{s_2}\big(T^{10}(L)-T^{10}(0)\big)\,dx^0=L(s_2-s_1)\neq0$ whenever $s_1<s_2$ and $L>0$. Thus $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ alone does not imply conservation of a slice integral; the vanishing side-flux hypothesis is indispensable, and the counterexample shows that the isolation clause of the integrated-conservation statement cannot be dropped from the integrated-conservation theorem.
before.strategy: Check the two divergence components directly; check the balance identity by computing the $x$-face integrals of $T^{10}$ over the slab, or by integrating $\partial_0T^{00}=-\partial_1T^{10}$ over $[s_1,s_2]\times[0,L]$. The construction is an explicit smooth symmetric tensor on the chart domain; it is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Divergence-free stress-energy with a nonconserved slice integral
after.statement: In an inertial chart on all of affine Minkowski space define the smooth symmetric field $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ everywhere, since the only possibly nonzero divergence components are $\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1-1=0$ and $\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0$. For $L>0$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, put $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$ and $K=[0,L]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$. The full spatial slice integral is $Q^0(s)=\int_K T^{00}(s,x)\,d^3x=A Ls$. The axis-one side-flux difference on a slab $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ is $\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^+}T^{10}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_1^-}T^{10}\,d^3x=-A L(s_2-s_1)$; all transverse fluxes vanish. Consequently [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] gives $Q^0(s_2)-Q^0(s_1)=A L(s_2-s_1)\ne0$ whenever $s_1<s_2$. For example $A=6,L=2,s_2-s_1=3$ gives $36$. Thus zero local divergence alone does not conserve a finite slice integral: the side-flux/isolation hypothesis of the integrated-conservation theorem cannot be dropped. This prescribed tensor is not claimed to arise from any selected matter model.
after.strategy: Compute the divergence components directly, then perform the full three-dimensional slice integration and the three-dimensional side-face integration. Both gain exactly the same transverse area A. The negative side-face difference gives the positive slice change through the finite-box theorem. No noncompact limit, physical model, or choice principle is used.

before.title: The box balance identity checked on an explicit stress-energy field
before.statement: In an inertial chart define the symmetric $(2,0)$ field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$ in the $(e_0,e_1)$ block and $0$ in all components involving $e_2$ or $e_3$ (equivalently $T=\tau^{\alpha\beta}\partial_\alpha\otimes\partial_\beta$ with $\tau$ the displayed $2\times2$ matrix). Then $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ has $f^0=\partial_0T^{00}+\partial_1T^{10}=1+1=2$ and $f^1=\partial_0T^{01}+\partial_1T^{11}=0$. For the box $B=[t_1,t_2]\times[x_1,x_2]$ (with the $e_2,e_3$ intervals arbitrary, the extra face integrals vanishing) the box identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(a) reads, for $b=0$, $$\int_B f^0\,d^2x=2(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$$ while the boundary terms on the $x^0$ faces contribute $(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$ and those on the $x^1$ faces contribute $(x_2-x_1)(t_2-t_1)$, which sum to the same value; for $b=1$ both sides vanish, the $x^0$-face terms $\pm\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x\,dx$ cancelling and the $x^1$-face terms $\pm\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^0\,dx^0$ cancelling. The example verifies the finite-flux identity exactly on a field with nonzero force density and no side-flux cancellation; no physical model is asserted for $T$.
before.strategy: Compute the four one-dimensional integrals on the faces with the outward sign convention of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] and compare with $\int_B f^b$; both computations are exact, using only the FTC and the displayed constants. No choice principle is used.

after.title: The box balance identity checked on an explicit stress-energy field
after.statement: In an inertial chart define the smooth symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$, with every other component zero. Its force density is $f^0=2$, $f^1=f^2=f^3=0$. Let $t_1<t_2$, $x_1<x_2$, $c_2<d_2$, $c_3<d_3$, and set $A=(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)>0$, $B=[t_1,t_2]\times[x_1,x_2]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$. For $b=0$, the full four-dimensional identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] reads $\int_B f^0\,d^4x=2A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$. The temporal-face difference is $A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$ and the axis-one-face difference is $A(t_2-t_1)(x_2-x_1)$; all transverse face terms vanish because $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$. For $b=1$, the temporal face integrals $\pm A\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^1\,dx^1$ cancel, as do the axis-one face integrals $\pm A\int_{t_1}^{t_2}x^0\,dx^0$, so both sides vanish; $b=2,3$ vanish identically. For example, transverse area $A=6$, temporal length $2$ and axis-one length $3$ give bulk integral $72$ and the nonzero face differences $36+36$. This verifies the finite-box identity on a field with nonzero force density and nonzero net side flux; no physical matter model is asserted.
after.strategy: Compute all integrals as three-dimensional face or four-dimensional volume Riemann integrals. Repeated integration of each transverse constant factor gives A, then the FTC computes the remaining integrals. For b=0 the two nonzero face differences add; for b=1 the two opposite-face pairs separately cancel; b=2,3 and all transverse faces vanish. The full finite-box theorem supplies the sign convention and repeated-integration framework. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Dust: conservation of rho n tensor n is equivalent to continuity and inertial flow
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with $\rho>0$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ field with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ everywhere (a future unit timelike field, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)), and set $T^{ab}:=\rho\,n^an^b$ (a $C^1$ symmetric $(2,0)$ field). Then, on $\Omega$, (a) $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ if and only if both $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ (continuity) and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ (inertial flow); (b) if $\rho\ge0$ is allowed to vanish, the implication $\partial_aT^{ab}=0\Rightarrow n^a\partial_an^b=0$ is asserted only on the open set $\{\rho>0\}$, and no assertion is made where $\rho=0$; (c) if $x:J\to A$ is a $C^2$ curve with $x'(s)=n(x(s))$ for all $s$ (an integral curve of $n$), then $x''(s)=0$: the flow lines of an inertial unit field are affine straight lines in the affine structure of $A$. The lemma is the exact mathematical content of the dust equations; it asserts no matter model, no interaction and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Expand $\partial_aT^{ab}=(\partial_a\rho)n^an^b+\rho(\partial_an^a)n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$ and rewrite the first two terms as $(\partial_a(\rho n^a))n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$. Contract with $n_b$ and use $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\partial_an^b=\tfrac12\partial_a(n_bn^b)=0$ to obtain $n_b\partial_aT^{ab}=-\partial_a(\rho n^a)$. Hence conservation gives continuity, and then the remaining horizontal part gives $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the converse is immediate. For (c), differentiate: $x''(s)=n^a\partial_an^b(x(s))=0$ by the chain rule, so $x'$ is constant and $x$ is affine. Source: the equivalence is the flat restriction of the dust computation of G6 and of the dust equations read off from (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong; the positivity hypothesis is stated because the converse needs it. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Dust: conservation of rho n tensor n is equivalent to continuity and inertial flow
after.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with $\rho>0$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ field which is future timelike and satisfies $\eta(n,n)=-1$ everywhere (a future unit timelike field, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)), and set $T^{ab}:=\rho\,n^an^b$ (a $C^1$ symmetric $(2,0)$ field). For the nonnegative-density branch in (b), the same conclusion holds for an integral curve whose image lies in $\{\rho>0\}$, under conservation there. The lemma is the exact mathematical content of the dust equations; it asserts no matter model, no interaction and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Expand $\partial_aT^{ab}=(\partial_a\rho)n^an^b+\rho(\partial_an^a)n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$ and rewrite the first two terms as $(\partial_a(\rho n^a))n^b+\rho n^a\partial_an^b$. Hence conservation gives continuity, and then the remaining horizontal part gives $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the converse is immediate. For (b), the same contraction gives continuity without dividing by $\rho$; the remaining term is $\rho n^a\partial_an^b=0$, so division is justified exactly where $\rho>0$. For (c), use the conservation antecedent to obtain inertial flow from (a), then differentiate: $x''(s)=n^a\partial_an^b(x(s))=0$ by the chain rule, so $x'$ is constant and $x$ is affine. before.title: Observer decomposition of a symmetric stress-energy tensor
before.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In the model's physical reading with $U=cn$, $\varepsilon$ is the energy density (joule per cubic metre) and $\pi$ the momentum density (kilogram per square metre per second) measured by the observer $U$, the mathematical content asserted here is the identity in (a) and the uniqueness in (b) alone. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Pointwise linear algebra. Since $h$ is the projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, and $\delta^a{}_c=h^a{}_c-n^an_c$, expand $T^{ab}=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)T^{cd}$ and use symmetry of $T$ to obtain (a) with the stated signs. For (b), contract (a) with $n_b$ using $n_bn^b=-1$, $n_b\pi^b=0$ and $S^{ab}n_b=0$; uniqueness follows by contracting a general decomposition with $n_an_b$ (gives $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$), with $h_{ac}h_{bd}$ (gives $S'=S$), and with $n_b$ (gives $\pi'=\pi$). No choice principle is used.

after.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $\Omega\subseteq A$ open, and let $T$ be a continuous symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c). At a point $p\in\Omega$ define $\varepsilon:=T^{ab}n_an_b$, $\pi^a:=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and $S^{ab}:=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Then: (a) $\pi$ lies in $n^\perp$, $S$ is symmetric and horizontal in both slots ($S^{ab}n_b=n_aS^{ab}=0$), and $$T^{ab}=\varepsilon\,n^an^b+c\,(n^a\pi^b+\pi^an^b)+S^{ab}.$$ (b) Contracting with $n$ gives $T^{ab}n_b=-\varepsilon n^a-c\pi^a$; hence $\varepsilon$ and $\pi$ are determined by $T$ and $n$, and the decomposition is unique among decompositions $T^{ab}=\varepsilon' n^an^b+c(n^a\pi'^b+\pi'^an^b)+S'^{ab}$ with $\pi'\in n^\perp$ and $S'$ symmetric horizontal: $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon$, $\pi'=\pi$, $S'=S$. (c) In any adapted inertial orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$, the numerical components of this decomposition are $\varepsilon=T^{00}$, $\pi^0=0$, $\pi^i=T^{0i}/c$ and $S^{0a}=S^{a0}=0$, $S^{ij}=T^{ij}$ for $i,j=1,2,3$. Define isotropic rest stress to mean $S^{ab}=p h^{ab}$ for a real scalar $p$, where $h^{ab}:=\eta^{ab}+n^an^b$. Thus $S=0$ means vanishing rest stress, and is the isotropic case $p=0$; isotropy permits any $p$, including nonzero pressure or tension. These are numerical tensor identities. Physical adoption of the energy/momentum-density reading is a separate model premise; this mathematical lemma asserts no observer measurement. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Pointwise linear algebra. Since $h$ is the projection of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, and $\delta^a{}_c=h^a{}_c-n^an_c$, expand $T^{ab}=(h^a{}_c-n^an_c)(h^b{}_d-n^bn_d)T^{cd}$ and use symmetry of $T$ to obtain (a) with the stated signs. No choice principle is used. For (c), in the adapted frame $n^a=\delta^a_0$, $n_a=-\delta_a^0$ and $h^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,1,1)$. Substituting these components into the definitions gives the stated entries. The rest-stress convention $S=p h$ gives $S^{ij}=p\delta^{ij}$ in that frame; it does not force $p=0$. The decomposition needs only continuity of $T$ and its pointwise symmetric tensor structure; no derivative or physical identification is used.

before.title: Divergence identity for the scalar-field stress-energy tensor
before.statement: In the setting of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]], with $\varphi$ smooth and $T$ the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action, $$\partial_aT^{ab}=K\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)\partial^b\varphi\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$ where $\partial^b=\eta^{bc}\partial_c$ and $\Box\varphi=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$. In particular the tensor is conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, exactly at the solutions of the scalar-field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$, and off shell the balance holds with the four-force density $f^b=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Expand $T^{ab}=K(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V))$: $\partial_a(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi)=(\Box\varphi)\partial^b\varphi+\partial^a\varphi\,\partial_a\partial^b\varphi$, and $\partial^b(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V)=\partial^c\varphi\,\partial^b\partial_c\varphi+V'(\varphi)\partial^b\varphi$; the two second-derivative terms cancel after relabeling by symmetry of mixed partials ([[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]) and $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=\Box$. Source: the direct divergence check is the flat-space restriction of the scalar computation in G6 of the research argument and of the analogous check (4.51) of Tong. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Divergence identity for the scalar-field stress-energy tensor
after.statement: In the setting of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]], with $\varphi$ smooth and $T$ the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action, $$\partial_aT^{ab}=K\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)\partial^b\varphi\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$ where $\partial^b=\eta^{bc}\partial_c$ and $\Box\varphi=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$. In particular every solution of the scalar-field equation $\Box\varphi=V\prime(\varphi)$ has conserved tensor, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar-field equation at every point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and hence throughout an open set on which $d\varphi$ is nowhere zero. In full generality conservation is equivalent to the pointwise product condition $(\Box\varphi-V\prime(\varphi))d\varphi=0$; it need not imply the scalar equation where $d\varphi=0$. Off shell the balance holds with the four-force density $f^b=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Expand $T^{ab}=K(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V))$: $\partial_a(\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi)=(\Box\varphi)\partial^b\varphi+\partial^a\varphi\,\partial_a\partial^b\varphi$, and $\partial^b(\tfrac12\partial_c\varphi\partial^c\varphi+V)=\partial^c\varphi\,\partial^b\partial_c\varphi+V'(\varphi)\partial^b\varphi$; the two second-derivative terms cancel after relabeling by symmetry of mixed partials ([[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]) and $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=\Box$. Source: the direct divergence check is the flat-space restriction of the scalar computation in G6 of the research argument and of the analogous check (4.51) of Tong. No choice principle is used. Write E=Box(phi)-Vprime(phi). The displayed identity is exact off shell. Since K>0 and the metric is nondegenerate, at a point with dphi nonzero at least one raised component partial^b phi is nonzero; zero divergence then forces E=0 there. At points with dphi=0 no such conclusion follows. For example phi=0 and V(s)=s give T=0, divergence zero, and E=-1 on any open Omega. Therefore the unconditional converse is false and is replaced by the exact product criterion and its noncritical-point converse.

before.title: Hodge reconstruction of an alternating two-tensor and the optional SI field split
before.statement: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); the two combinations are the independent quadratic invariants of $F$. (d) (Optional SI identification.) If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for spatial vector fields $E,B$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Work in the oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)): write $F_{0i}=-e_i$ (this defines $e_i$ through $F_{i0}$), and the spatial block determines a three-vector $b$ by $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; antisymmetry fixes all components. Evaluate $(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ componentwise using $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]) to obtain $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$ and the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$; verify $*^2=-1$ on the six basis bivectors by direct evaluation. The invariant formulas follow by expanding in this frame; the boost law follows from the tensor component law [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) applied to $F$ under the passive boost $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] ([[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]), substituting the SI identifications. Sources: the tensor component law and the Hodge-star algebra are the flat restriction of S8 of the research supplier argument; the duality conventions and the field-strength components are documented in Carroll Chapter 1 pp. 16-24 and Tong 4.5.1. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Hodge reconstruction of an alternating two-tensor and the optional SI field split
after.statement: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Use the standard form normalization $F=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}F_{ab}\theta^a\wedge\theta^b$ in the dual coframe $\theta^a(e_b)=\delta^a_b$ of an oriented orthonormal frame, and define $(F\wedge F)(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3):=2[F(v_0,v_1)F(v_2,v_3)-F(v_0,v_2)F(v_1,v_3)+F(v_0,v_3)F(v_1,v_2)]$, the alternating four-form exterior square. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); also $F\wedge F=2(e\cdot b)\varepsilon$. The two scalar expressions $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ form a basis of the homogeneous quadratic polynomials in the six components of $F$ invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; the square-wedge expression is dependent, $F\wedge F=-\tfrac12 I_2\varepsilon$. $I_2$ is an oriented pseudoscalar and changes sign if the chosen orientation is reversed with the metric and $F$ held fixed. (d) (Optional SI identification.) Let $c>0$. If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for spatial vector fields $E,B$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and $F\wedge F=-2(E\cdot B)\varepsilon/c$. If $\kappa:=(F\wedge F)(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=(F\wedge F)_{0123}$, then $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. Under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta\in(-1,1)$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ where the cross product is the right-handed product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: First obtain an oriented rest frame adapted to $n$: the observer decomposition theorem proves $n^\perp$ is a three-dimensional positive inner-product space ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)); apply finite Gram–Schmidt to a basis of it ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]) and reverse one spatial basis vector if the resulting frame orientation is negative. This uses only finite choices. Let $a_i=\theta^0\wedge\theta^i$ and $s_1=\theta^2\wedge\theta^3$, $s_2=\theta^3\wedge\theta^1$, $s_3=\theta^1\wedge\theta^2$. The declared dual and volume conventions give $*a_i=-s_i$, $*s_i=a_i$ by direct component evaluation. Thus $*^2=-1$ on all six basis forms, $F=-e_i a_i-b_i s_i$ and $*F=-b_i a_i+e_i s_i$, proving the annihilation, six-component recovery and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$. Raise the time-spatial indices with the diagonal metric and count both orders of each skew pair to get $\frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4e\cdot b$. The explicitly normalized square wedge has $a_i\wedge s_i=\varepsilon$ and all unmatched terms zero, so $F\wedge F=2e\cdot b\,\varepsilon$; the witness $F_{01}=F_{23}=1$ gives $e_1=b_1=-1$ and square wedge $+2\varepsilon$. The tensor/volume laws ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),(v)) show that these expressions are invariant under proper Lorentz changes. For completeness of the quadratic invariant claim, spatial half-turns force the three coefficient blocks of a rotation-invariant quadratic polynomial to be diagonal, and proper axis permutations force scalar diagonals; it has the form $A|e|^2+B|b|^2+C e\cdot b$. For $e=(0,1,0),b=0$, an axis-one passive boost gives $e'=(0,\gamma,0),b'=(0,0,\gamma\beta)$; invariance gives $A(\gamma^2-1)+B\gamma^2\beta^2=0$, whence $A+B=0$ for any nonzero allowed $\beta$. Both surviving invariant polynomials are linearly independent by testing $b=0,e\ne0$ and $e=b\ne0$. For the optional SI identification, apply the actual passive boost matrix to the two raised indices of $F$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). All six entries are $E'_1=E_1$, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-vB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+vB_2)$, $B'_1=B_1$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+vE_3/c^2)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-vE_2/c^2)$, which are exactly the promised vector formulas with the right-handed cross product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Substituting $e=-E/c,b=B$ gives the displayed invariants and standard four-form coefficient $\kappa=-2E\cdot B/c$, hence $E\cdot B=-c\kappa/2$. The zero-boost case gives $\gamma=1$ directly. All arguments are finite-dimensional, choice-free algebra and assert no EM dynamics. The cached Carroll full-text equations (1.79)–(1.88), printed pp.21–23, were read for wedge normalization and the Lorentzian star-square rule; the S8 local research route is independently recomputed, not accepted by citation.

before.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
before.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $n$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. Then $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ because $n$ is constant, so $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ is conserved by [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. If $\rho_0$ is supported in the spatial box $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$, the slice integrals $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ satisfy $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for all $s_1<s_2$ by [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c), since $T$ is time-independent and its spatial side flux through the faces of $\bar K$ vanishes. The flow lines are the parallel straight lines $x^1=\beta x^0+\mathrm{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. The example exhibits a family of exact solutions of the dust equations; it asserts no interaction and no measurement.
before.strategy: Verify $\eta(n,n)=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=-1$ and both dust equations as displayed; conservation and the slice constancy follow from [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]] and [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) applied on a slab whose spatial box contains $\operatorname{supp}\rho_0$. This is an explicit computation in the page's framework. No choice principle is used.

after.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
after.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $n$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. Then $n^a\partial_a\rho=\gamma(\partial_0\rho+\beta\partial_1\rho)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$ because $n$ is constant, so $(\rho,n)$ satisfies the dust equations and $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ is conserved by [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. For any finite spatial box $\bar K=[c_1,d_1]\times[c_2,d_2]\times[c_3,d_3]$ whose slab lies in the chart domain, the finite slice integrals $Q^b(s)=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)d^3x$ are constant in $s$, because $T^{0b}$ is time independent. This also follows from the slice-balance identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b): $T^{2b}=T^{3b}=0$, and the two $x^1$-face fluxes $T^{1b}=\rho_0\gamma\beta n^b$ agree pointwise and cancel with opposite orientations. The individual $x^1$-face flux need not vanish. A nonzero transverse profile is not compactly supported in all three spatial variables, since it is independent of $x^1$. The nonnegative variant $\rho_0\ge0$, including compact support in the transverse $(x^2,x^3)$ plane, gives the same exact conserved solution and finite-box constancy, with the zero-density qualification of [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]\,(b). The flow lines are the parallel straight lines $x^1=\beta x^0+\mathrm{const}$, $x^2,x^3$ constant. The example exhibits a family of exact solutions of the dust equations; it asserts no interaction and no measurement.
after.strategy: Verify $\eta(n,n)=-\gamma^2+\gamma^2\beta^2=-1$. Since $n$ is constant, $\partial_an^b=0$ and $\partial_an^a=0$; since $\rho$ depends only on $x^2,x^3$, $n^a\partial_a\rho=0$. Hence both dust equations hold, including for the nonnegative-profile variant, and [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]] gives conservation. On any finite spatial box, $T^{0b}=\gamma\rho_0 n^b$ is continuous and independent of $x^0$, so its finite integral is constant. In the exact slice identity [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b), the divergence term vanishes; the $x^2,x^3$ terms vanish separately and the $x^1$ terms cancel because the integrands and their transverse integration domains are equal on both faces. Clause (c), which requires each side flux to vanish, is not used. The integral curves have constant tangent $n$, hence the stated parallel affine lines. The entire calculation uses prescribed fields and no matter-model or empirical assertion. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
before.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have rest energy density $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed energy density $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ carries one factor of $\gamma$ from the increased energy of each dust particle and one from the contracted volume, as in the source computation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
before.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
after.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have constant rest coefficient $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed coordinate coefficient $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ is the numerical factorization $\gamma^2\rho=\gamma(\gamma\rho)$. Its source interpretation as one energy factor and one volume factor belongs to the separately adopted dust model reading; it is not an empirical identification proved by this component calculation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
after.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
before.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field, $\partial_a\varphi=f'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)k_a$ and $\Box\varphi=k^ak_af''(k_ax^a+\theta_0)=0$, so $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]. Its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ symmetric, future-null directed, with $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. In an inertial frame $T^{00}=Kf'^2(k^0)^2\ge0$. The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model; it asserts no wave observation and no measurement.
before.strategy: Substitute $\partial_a\varphi=f'k_a$ into the Hilbert tensor formula of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]; the potential term drops and $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$ kills the trace term, leaving $Kf'^2k^ak^b$. The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. Source: the scalar stress tensor (4.51) of Tong with V=0; the null-covector condition is the framework's own. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
after.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. In either case one has $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. after.strategy: Substitute $\partial_a\varphi=f'k_a$ into the Hilbert tensor formula of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]; the potential term drops and $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$ kills the trace term, leaving $Kf'^2k^ak^b$. The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. The coefficient $Kf\prime{}^2$ is strictly positive exactly where $f\prime\ne0$ and vanishes exactly where $f\prime=0$, because $K>0$. Since $k^\sharp$ is a fixed nonzero future-null vector, this proves the precise rank-one/zero alternative. Squaring $k_an^a$ gives the nonnegative observer contraction stated without any claim that the zero tensor is future null.

before.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
before.statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of the affine Minkowski space A and let n: Omega -> V be an observer congruence with acceleration a := nabla_n n, expansion tensor theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and rest metric h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a)-(c), def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space). (a) Material family and material metric. Let J be a nonempty open interval, B a nonempty open subset of R^3, and Phi: J x B -> Omega a smooth map with partial Phi/partial s = n(Phi(s,xi)) for all (s,xi) in J x B; assume that Phi is an injective immersion (its derivative is injective at every point), so that the four vector fields n, e_1, e_2, e_3 are linearly independent, where e_I := partial Phi/partial xi^I, I = 1,2,3. Define the material metric G_{IJ}(s,xi) := h(e_I,e_J) evaluated at Phi(s,xi). Then G is symmetric, and for every s the matrix (G_{IJ}) is positive definite, so that G(.,.) is a Riemannian metric on B for each s; moreover (s,xi) |-> G_{IJ}(s,xi) is smooth. (b) Evolution of rest separations. For all I,J and every (s,xi) one has d/ds G_{IJ} = (L_n h)(e_I,e_J) = 2 theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b, equivalently d/dtau G_{IJ} = 2 c theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b, where tau = s/c is the proper time of the congruence worldlines (the flow lines of n have four-velocity c n). If additionally I = J and e_I is nowhere zero on the family, then with |e_I|_h := sqrt(h(e_I,e_I)) and u := e_I/|e_I|_h one has d/dtau |e_I|_h = c theta(u,u) |e_I|_h: the fractional rate of change, per unit proper time, of the rest length of the material element in the direction e_I is c theta(u,u), positive where the expansion is positive and negative where it is negative. (c) Born rigidity. If theta = 0 on Omega, i.e. the congruence is Born rigid, then G is constant along the flow, d/ds G_{IJ}(s,xi) = 0 for all I,J,s,xi and with no restriction on the separation: a Born-rigid material continuum preserves its internal metric exactly. Conversely, if theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b is nonzero at some point of the family, then the corresponding component G_{IJ} is not constant there. (d) Scope. Everything is local on the given smooth family and uses only the flat connection and the congruence kinematics. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem or boundary condition is used, and no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Differentiate the material metric along the flow. By construction e_I = Phi_* partial_{xi^I} and n = Phi_* partial_s are pushforwards of the commuting coordinate fields of J x B, so [n,e_I] = 0 (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields, prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket). For any (0,2) tensor field K and vector fields X,Y the Lie derivative identity (L_X K)(Y,Z) = X(K(Y,Z)) - K([X,Y],Z) - K(Y,[X,Z]) together with [n,e_I] = [n,e_J] = 0 gives d/ds [h(e_I,e_J)] = n(h(e_I,e_J)) = (L_n h)(e_I,e_J) (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). Clause (d) of def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics states (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, hence d/ds G_{IJ} = 2 theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b. The proper-time form uses d/dtau = c d/ds: the flow is parametrized by s with dx/ds = n, so the four-velocity is c n and ds = c dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, def-sr-proper-time, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)). The length statement is the chain rule applied to |e_I|_h^2 = h(e_I,e_I): d/ds |e_I|_h = (1/(2|e_I|_h)) 2 theta(e_I,e_I) = |e_I|_h theta(u,u) with u := e_I/|e_I|_h and theta(u,u) = theta(e_I,e_I)/|e_I|_h^2 (def-derivative, thm-algebra-of-derivatives, thm-chain-rule). Positive definiteness: h is symmetric with radical spanned by n and positive definite on n^perp (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a)); for v = v^I e_I nonzero and not parallel to n one has h(v,v) > 0, so G is positive definite, and no v^I e_I can be parallel to n because n, e_1, e_2, e_3 are linearly independent by the injective-immersion hypothesis. Smoothness of (s,xi) |-> G_{IJ} follows from smoothness of Phi, of n and of the bilinear form eta (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, def-sr-affine-minkowski-model). The Born-rigid case is the vanishing of theta. No choice principle is used.

after.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
after.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:
$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$
where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define
$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$
These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is Born rigid when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.
(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.
(b) For all $I,J$,
$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$
where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and
$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$
The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.
(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighborhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.
(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.
after.strategy:
Use only first derivatives of $n$ and two derivatives of $\Phi$. The coordinate rules are tensorial under constant Lorentz changes of inertial coordinates by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]; for smooth data they agree with the established smooth definitions. Differentiating $\eta(n,n)=-1$ gives $n_b\partial_an^b=0$, hence $\eta(n,a)=0$. Expansion of the projected symmetrization gives
$$2\theta_{ab}=\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+a_an_b.$$
Differentiating $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ in the displayed first-order Lie formula gives exactly this right side, proving $L_nh=2\theta$. The projectors make $\theta$ horizontal in both slots.
For the material fields, equality of the mixed partials of $C^2$ components of $\Phi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the total chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) give
$$\partial_se_I^a=\partial_{\xi^I}n^a(\Phi)=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b.$$
Differentiating $G_{IJ}=h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ by the product rule gives the displayed coordinate formula for $(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)$, and thus $\partial_sG_{IJ}=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$. This direct calculation does not invoke a smooth-only Lie-bracket supplier for $C^1$ fields. In the smooth branch, the same mixed-partial identity is the usual commuting material-coordinate calculation $[n,e_I]=0$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]), and recovers the original smooth route.
The derivative of $\Phi$ has four independent columns by immersion, so no nonzero linear combination of the three $e_I$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(n)$. The rest projection has that one-dimensional kernel and is positive definite on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c)); hence $G$ is positive definite. $h(\Phi)$ and $e_I$ are $C^1$, so $G$ is $C^1$, and smooth if all data are smooth. Along a flow line $\partial_s\Phi=n$ is nonzero future timelike, and the proper-time definition gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-\eta(n,n)}/c=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Apply the chain rule to $\ell_I^2=G_{II}$: $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(e_I,e_I)/\ell_I$. Since $h(e_I)-e_I$ is parallel to $n$, horizontality gives $\theta(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2\theta(u_I,u_I)$, proving the fractional-rate formula. If $\theta=0$, the interval zero-derivative corollary [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] proves constancy for each fixed label. A nonzero derivative prevents local constancy. All claims, including the smooth special case, are proved with the stated finite regularity and no zero tangent is called timelike.

before.title: Perfect fluid: conservation is equivalent to the energy and Euler equations
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) and set $T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$. Write $D\varepsilon:=n^a\partial_a\varepsilon$, $\vartheta:=\partial_an^a$, $a^b:=n^a\partial_an^b$ and $h^{bc}:=\eta^{bc}+n^bn^c$ (the expansion scalar, acceleration and rest projector of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] for the congruence $n$ and the flat derivative of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]). Then the identity $$\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)+\big((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP\big)$$ holds on $\Omega$, and consequently $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta=0$ and $(\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP=0$ on $\Omega$. The two equations are the energy-balance and Euler equations of the model; the lemma asserts no equation of state, no thermodynamic relation and no causality condition. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]n^b+(\varepsilon+P)n^a\partial_an^b+\partial^bP$, rewrite $\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]=D\varepsilon+DP+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta$ with $DP=n^a\partial_aP$, and decompose $\partial^bP=h^{bc}\partial_cP-n^bDP$ because $\eta^{bc}=h^{bc}-n^bn^c$; the terms in $DP$ cancel, leaving the displayed identity. Contracting with $n_b$ gives $-\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)$ and projecting with $h$ gives the second bracket, so the two equations are equivalent to conservation. Source: the flat restriction of the perfect-fluid computation of G6 and of (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong. No choice principle is used.

after.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $\varepsilon,P:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) and set $T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$. Write $D\varepsilon:=n^a\partial_a\varepsilon$, $\vartheta:=\partial_an^a$, $a^b:=n^a\partial_an^b$ and $h^{bc}:=\eta^{bc}+n^bn^c$ (these formulas define the first-order expansion scalar, acceleration and raised rest projection for the stipulated $C^1$ field; they agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] and [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] when the field is smooth). Then the identity $$\partial_aT^{ab}=n^b\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)+\big((\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP\big)$$ holds on $\Omega$, and consequently $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$ if and only if $D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta=0$ and $(\varepsilon+P)a^b+h^{bc}\partial_cP=0$ on $\Omega$. The two equations are the energy-balance and Euler equations of the model; the lemma asserts no equation of state, no thermodynamic relation and no causality condition. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Compute $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]n^b+(\varepsilon+P)n^a\partial_an^b+\partial^bP$, rewrite $\partial_a[(\varepsilon+P)n^a]=D\varepsilon+DP+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta$ with $DP=n^a\partial_aP$, and decompose $\partial^bP=h^{bc}\partial_cP-n^bDP$ because $\eta^{bc}=h^{bc}-n^bn^c$; the terms in $DP$ cancel, leaving the displayed identity. The second bracket is horizontal: $n_ba^b=\tfrac12n^a\partial_a(\eta(n,n))=0$ and $n_bh^{bc}=0$. Contracting with $n_b$ gives $-\big(D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+P)\vartheta\big)$ and projecting with $h$ gives the second bracket, so the two equations are equivalent to conservation. Source: the flat restriction of the perfect-fluid computation of G6 and of (4.53)-(4.55) of Tong. No choice principle is used. This argument divides by neither $\varepsilon+P$ nor $P$: the degenerate case $\varepsilon+P=0$ is retained. All quantities use at most first coordinate derivatives of the $C^1$ fields.

before.title: Counterexample: no speed-independent uniform low-speed remainder for the kinetic energy
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("rem failure at relativistic/null speeds"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08 ("constants depend on z_0")
before.design_state: complete refutation by the explicit family gamma = n with the exact difference formula
before.statement:
**Statement refuted.** Let $c>0$ and $m>0$. There is a real $B\ge0$ such that $|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2|\le B$ for every future unit $n\in V$, every $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and the relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), where $T_n$ is the kinetic energy of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

**Counterexample.** For every integer $N\ge2$ choose a unit vector $e\in n^\perp$ for a fixed future unit $n$ (possible because $n^\perp$ is a three-dimensional real subspace on which the restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite, so every nonzero vector of $n^\perp$ may be divided by its norm, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)) and put $$w_N:=c\sqrt{1-N^{-2}}\;e,\qquad U_N:=N\Bigl(n+\frac{w_N}{c}\Bigr),\qquad P_N:=mU_N .$$ Then $|w_N|^2=c^2(1-N^{-2})<c^2$, and $\eta(U_N,U_N)=N^2(-1+|w_N|^2/c^2)=-1$ with $U_N$ future timelike, so $U_N$ is a future timelike unit (in the normalization $\eta(U_N,U_N)=-1$) vector; the relative velocity and Lorentz factor of $U_N$ are $w_N$ and $N$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P_N)=mc^2(N-1)$ together with $\tfrac12m|w_N|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-N^{-2})$. Hence $$T_n(P_N)-\tfrac12m|w_N|^2=mc^2\Bigl(N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2}\Bigr),$$ which exceeds any prescribed real $B$ for all sufficiently large $N$; equivalently the relative deviation $\frac{T_n(P_N)-\frac12m|w_N|^2}{\frac12m|w_N|^2}=\frac{(2N+1)(N-1)}{N+1}$ is unbounded in $N$. Therefore the refuted statement is false for every pair $(c,m)$, and any valid low-speed error bound must depend on the admissible speed domain (the constants $K(z_0)$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] do). The construction is a statement about the stipulated model and contains no empirical claim.
before.strategy: Assume the refuted statement and derive a contradiction. Fix a future unit $n$ and $e\in n^\perp$ with $|e|=1$; for each $N\ge2$ set $a_N:=c\sqrt{1-N^{-2}}$, $w_N:=a_Ne$ and $U_N:=N(n+w_N/c)$. By [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) $\eta(n,w_N)=0$ and $\eta(w_N,w_N)=a_N^2$, so $\eta(U_N,U_N)=N^2(\eta(n,n)+2\eta(n,w_N)/c+\eta(w_N,w_N)/c^2)=N^2(-1+a_N^2/c^2)=-1$, and $U_N$ is future timelike; clause (d) of the same theorem then identifies $w_N=c\,h(U_N)/\gamma$ with $\gamma=N$, because $\gamma=-\eta(U_N/c,n)=N$. Applying [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) to $P_N=mU_N$ gives $T_n(P_N)=mc^2(N-1)$, $|w_N|^2=c^2(1-N^{-2})$ and the displayed difference; the relative deviation is the quotient of these expressions, namely $\frac{(2N+1)(N-1)}{N+1}$ (verified by multiplying out). Since $N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2}\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$ in the ordered field $\mathbb R$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-of-abs-value]] conventions), for every real $B$ there is $N$ with $mc^2(N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2})>B$, contradicting the assumed uniform bound. The norms and the causality classification are those of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]] and [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] for the model [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

before.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
before.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that in the primed frame the fluid moves with speed $v=\beta c$ in the negative $x'^1$ direction), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the observer at rest in the primed frame measures the energy density $T'(e_0',e_0')=T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$, which differs from the rest-frame density $\varepsilon$ unless $\beta=0$ and is at least $\varepsilon$ when $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; the transverse diagonal components stay equal to the pressure $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to read $T'^{00}$ as an energy density; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
before.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The energy-density reading is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Uniform low-speed expansion of the observer energy, momentum and kinetic energy of a massive four-momentum
before.design_state: complete transport of the Taylor remainder through the mass-shell identities with uniform constants depending only on the speed bound
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U\in V$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)$ and $m(P)$ be the observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], and let $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ be the Lorentz factor and relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d); then $u:=U/c$ satisfies $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $m(P)=m$.

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$, suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $f,R$ be as in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]], so that $\gamma=f(z)$ and $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$. Then:

(a) $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ for the common real number $R_E:=mc^2R(z)$, and $$|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2=K(z_0)\,\frac{m|w|^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\Bigr|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,\tfrac12m|w|^2 .$$

(b) $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with $R_q:=m(\gamma-1)w$, and $$|R_q|\le m|w|\Bigl(\frac z2+K(z_0)z^2\Bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac12+K(z_0)z_0\Bigr)z\,m|w| ;$$ moreover $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$.

(c) Every constant above depends only on $z_0$, so the estimates are uniform over all future unit $n$, all $m>0$ and all $P=mU$ with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$; if $z=0$ (equivalently $w=0$, $U=cn$) then $R_E=R_q=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$, $q_n(P)=0$ and $T_n(P)=0$. The lemma is a statement about the mathematical model only; it asserts no measured quantity, no approximation of a physical theory and no error estimate for any experiment.
before.strategy:
Combine [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) and [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]. Since $z=|w|^2/c^2$, clause (d) of the theorem gives $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=(1-z)^{-1/2}=f(z)$, hence $\gamma-1=\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$.

(a) Multiply by $mc^2$: $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+mc^2R(z)$, because $mc^2\cdot\tfrac z2=\tfrac12mc^2z=\tfrac12m|w|^2$; and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]\,(b), so the same remainder occurs. The bound $|mc^2R(z)|\le mc^2K(z_0)z^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the first display, and $2K(z_0)z\cdot\tfrac12m|w|^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the second.

after.title: Uniform low-speed expansion of the observer energy, momentum and kinetic energy of a massive four-momentum
after.design_state: complete transport of the Taylor remainder through the mass-shell identities with uniform constants depending only on the speed bound
after.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U\in V$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)$ and $m(P)$ be the observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], put $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c), and let $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=h(U)/\gamma=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ be the Lorentz factor and relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d); then $u:=U/c$ satisfies $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $m(P)=m$.

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$, suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $f,R$ be as in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]], so that $\gamma=f(z)$ and $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$. Then:

(b) $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with $R_q:=m(\gamma-1)w$, and $$|R_q|\le m|w|\Bigl(\frac z2+K(z_0)z^2\Bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac12+K(z_0)z_0\Bigr)z\,m|w| ;$$ moreover $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$.

The lemma is a statement about the mathematical model only; it asserts no measured quantity, no approximation of a physical theory and no error estimate for any experiment.

before.title: Fermi-Walker transport preserves the metric, and explicit rigid and non-rigid observer congruences
before.statement: (a) Preservation. Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline and let X,Y: I -> V be C^1 Fermi-Walker transported fields along x (def-sr-fermi-walker-transport). Then tau |-> eta(X(tau),Y(tau)) is constant on I; in particular Fermi-Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi-Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c is an orthonormal tetrad (E_0(tau),...,E_3(tau)) at every tau with E_0(tau) = U(tau)/c (observer-adapted tetrad), by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Rindler wedge congruence. In an inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. Then Phi is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge W := {(x^0,x) : x > |x^0|}, with smooth inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)); the pullback of eta is g = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2; the field n := rho^{-1} partial/partial theta is a future unit timelike field on W whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial/partial rho, hence eta(a,a) = rho^{-2}; its rest slices theta = const are hyperplanes orthogonal to n with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 independent of theta; and the frame (n, partial/partial rho, partial/partial y, partial/partial z) is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since [n, partial/partial rho] = +(1/rho) n is nonzero (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). (c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy. Fix real Omega. In the inertial chart let U_Omega be the open timelike region r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/Omega^2 when Omega!=0, and the whole chart when Omega=0. On this four-dimensional open set put K=partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2), gamma(r)=(1-Omega^2 r^2/c^2)^(-1/2), and n=gamma(r)K. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If Omega!=0, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If Omega=0, n=partial_0 is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are x^0=const. Now fix R>0 with |Omega|R<c and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder r=R, x^3=const, whose rotating angle is varphi=phi-Omega t modulo2pi, x^0=ct. The ring observer phi=phi_0+Omega t has n=gamma(R)(1,-(Omega R/c)sin phi,(Omega R/c)cos phi,0). The induced metric is -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies dt/dvarphi=Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at t=0 has signed time offset Delta t=2pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). For Omega!=0 it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For Omega=0 the offset is zero and ring rest lines are t=const. (d) Bell congruence. Let q: J -> R^3 be C^2 with q(t) = (q_1(t),0,0) and |q_1'(t)| < c, and consider the congruence of translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (c t, q(t) + xi) parametrized by xi in an open subset of R^3, with n = gamma(1, q_1'(t)/c, 0, 0), gamma = (1 - q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and unit longitudinal rest vector s = gamma(q_1'(t)/c, 1, 0, 0). Then theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q_1'(t) q_1''(t)/c^3, which is nonzero exactly when q_1'(t) q_1''(t) is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with q_1'(t) q_1''(t) nonzero, although for every fixed chart time t the separation between the members labelled xi_1 and xi_2 is the constant |xi_1 - xi_2|. A breaking or fracture conclusion about a material rod would additionally require an elasticity model and a failure criterion and is not a kinematic statement.
before.strategy: (a) For Fermi-Walker transported X,Y, d/dtau eta(X,Y) = eta(X',Y) + eta(X,Y') and substituting X' = c^{-2}(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A) and the analogous expression for Y' gives c^{-2}[eta(A,X)eta(U,Y) - eta(U,X)eta(A,Y) + eta(A,Y)eta(U,X) - eta(U,Y)eta(A,X)] = 0. The initial-tetrad family therefore remains orthonormal, and E_0 = U/c is transported by def-sr-fermi-walker-transport (b); uniqueness is lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Injectivity of Phi follows from x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and the sign of x; the inverse formulas are the standard hyperbolic identities cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 and tanh(theta) = x^0/x, and both maps are smooth on their domains because rho > 0 and x - x^0 > 0. Differentiating Phi gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta, dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so -(dx^0)^2 + dx^2 = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2. The field n is unit future by inspection; a direct computation with the metric gives nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and hence a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho; the rest slices are the theta-level sets, orthogonal to n because the metric has no theta-rho cross term, with the displayed induced metric independent of theta, so theta_{ab} = 0 and, since the slice is orthogonal to a field whose rest distribution is integrable, omega = 0; the commutator is [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2)partial_theta = +(1/rho)n. (c) K is future timelike exactly on the stated U_Omega and is Killing by direct coordinate differentiation. Projecting the symmetric derivative of n=gamma K to its rest space kills the derivative-of-gamma terms (K is parallel to n) and the Killing terms, so theta=0. Put kappa=eta(K,.)=-dx^0+(Omega/c)(x^1 dx^2-x^2 dx^1). Then d kappa=2(Omega/c)dx^1 wedge dx^2 and kappa wedge d kappa=-2(Omega/c)dx^0 wedge dx^1 wedge dx^2, nonzero exactly when Omega!=0. Since n-flat=gamma kappa, n-flat wedge d(n-flat)=gamma^2 kappa wedge d kappa; the stated ambient Frobenius/vorticity result follows, including at the axis by these smooth Cartesian formulas. The Omega=0 limit has the constant unit field. On the ring cylinder, substitute x^0=ct, x^1=Rcos(varphi+Omega t), x^2=Rsin(varphi+Omega t) to obtain the displayed metric and covector. Its one-dimensional kernel is the line field generated by partial_varphi+[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]partial_t, whose integral gives the signed holonomy. A globally defined time-oriented rest-synchronization function would have differential a positive multiple of dt-[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]dvarphi. Its integral around a fixed-t ring would have nonzero constant sign for Omega!=0, contradicting exactness of that differential. No local nonintegrability is attributed to the cylinder's one-dimensional rest-line field. (d) Write beta=q_1'/c, beta'=q_1''/c, x^0=ct and n_b=(-gamma,gamma beta,0,0), so partial_0=(1/c)d/dt and partial_1 n_b=0. Differentiation gives partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 beta beta'/c and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 beta'/c, using 1+gamma^2 beta^2=gamma^2. Contract with s=(gamma beta,gamma,0,0): s^0[s^0 partial_0 n_0+s^1 partial_0 n_1]=gamma^5 beta beta'(1-beta^2)/c=gamma^3 beta beta'/c=gamma^3 q_1' q_1''/c^3. Projection to the rest space does not change this contraction since s is rest-orthogonal. All transverse expansion components vanish, so it is nonzero exactly under the stated condition, and fixed chart-time separations remain xi_1-xi_2. The material fracture conclusion is excluded. All computations use finite algebra and the declared calculus, with no choice principle.

Projecting the symmetric derivative of n=gamma K to its rest space kills the derivative-of-gamma terms (K is parallel to n) and the Killing terms, so theta=0. Put kappa=eta(K,.)=-dx^0+(Omega/c)(x^1 dx^2-x^2 dx^1). Then d kappa=2(Omega/c)dx^1 wedge dx^2 and kappa wedge d kappa=-2(Omega/c)dx^0 wedge dx^1 wedge dx^2, nonzero exactly when Omega!=0. Since n-flat=gamma kappa, n-flat wedge d(n-flat)=gamma^2 kappa wedge d kappa; the stated ambient Frobenius/vorticity result follows, including at the axis by these smooth Cartesian formulas. The Omega=0 limit has the constant unit field. On the ring cylinder, substitute x^0=ct, x^1=Rcos(varphi+Omega t), x^2=Rsin(varphi+Omega t) to obtain the displayed metric and covector. Its one-dimensional kernel is the line field generated by partial_varphi+[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]partial_t, whose integral gives the signed holonomy. A globally defined time-oriented rest-synchronization function would have differential a positive multiple of dt-[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]dvarphi. Its integral around a fixed-t ring would have nonzero constant sign for Omega!=0, contradicting exactness of that differential. No local nonintegrability is attributed to the cylinder's one-dimensional rest-line field. (d) C2 q makes q1' C1, gamma C1 and n C1. Use the explicitly given first-order projected symmetric derivative of n; no smooth-only congruence or later connecting-field theorem is invoked. Write beta=q_1'/c, beta'=q_1''/c, x^0=ct and n_b=(-gamma,gamma beta,0,0), so partial_0=(1/c)d/dt and partial_1 n_b=0. Differentiation gives partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 beta beta'/c and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 beta'/c, using 1+gamma^2 beta^2=gamma^2. Contract with s=(gamma beta,gamma,0,0): s^0[s^0 partial_0 n_0+s^1 partial_0 n_1]=gamma^5 beta beta'(1-beta^2)/c=gamma^3 beta beta'/c=gamma^3 q_1' q_1''/c^3. Projection to the rest space does not change this contraction since s is rest-orthogonal. All transverse expansion components vanish, so it is nonzero exactly under the stated condition, and fixed chart-time separations remain xi_1-xi_2. The material fracture conclusion is excluded. All computations use finite algebra and the declared calculus, with no choice principle.

before.title: Bell congruence worked: rest separation grows as gamma(t)L while the chart separation stays constant
before.statement: Worked computation for the Bell congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d) and the material metric of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching. Fix c > 0 and alpha > 0, let J := (-c/alpha, c/alpha), put q(t) := (1/2) alpha t^2 on J and let x_xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + xi, 0, 0) for xi in an open interval containing [0,L], L > 0, in the inertial chart x with x^0 = c t. Then |q'(t)| = alpha|t| < c on the two-sided domain J; write beta(t) := alpha t/c and gamma(t) := (1 - beta(t)^2)^{-1/2}. (a) The translated congruence field is n = gamma (1, beta, 0, 0) and the material field e := partial_xi is the constant (0,1,0,0); since eta(n,e) = gamma beta, the h-length of e is |e|_h = sqrt(eta(e,e) + eta(n,e)^2) = sqrt(1 + gamma^2 beta^2) = gamma(t) (lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a), thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d)). Hence the rest separation between the rockets labelled 0 and L is |e|_h L = gamma(t) L > L for every t != 0, with minimum L at t = 0, while the chart-frame separation is q(t) + L - q(t) = L for every t in J. (b) The longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence is theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3, with unit rest vector s = gamma(beta,1,0,0) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d)); it vanishes at t = 0 and is nonzero for every t != 0, negative for t < 0 and positive for t > 0. By lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (b) the internal longitudinal material metric component is G_11 = h(e,e) = gamma(t)^2 and its derivatives are d/ds G_11 = 2 theta(e,e) and d/dtau G_11 = 2 c theta(e,e); equivalently the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is d/dtau log(gamma L) = c theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^2, and d(gamma L)/d tau = gamma^4 L alpha^2 t/c^2. (c) Explicit check at alpha t = 3c/5, i.e. t = 3c/(5alpha) in J: beta = 3/5, gamma = 5/4 and sinh and cosh are not needed; the rest separation is 5L/4 > L, the internal metric component is G_11 = 25/16 > 1, the expansion is theta(s,s) = (125/64)(3alpha/(5c^2)) = 75alpha/(64c^2), and the fractional rest-separation rate is c theta(s,s) = 75alpha/(64c). At t = 0 the rest separation takes its minimum L and the expansion vanishes; the domain is the two-sided interval (-c/alpha, c/alpha), so both the decelerating branch t < 0 (negative expansion) and the accelerating branch t > 0 (positive expansion) are included. (d) Scope. The computation is exact kinematics of the specified family: it uses no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no force law, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it draws no conclusion about real threads; no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Direct evaluation of the family in the two-sided subluminal domain. (a) Differentiating the members with the chain rule gives tangent (c, q'(t), 0, 0) = (c/gamma) n, so the flow field is n = gamma(1, beta, 0, 0) and each member is future timelike (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, thm-chain-rule); the h-length computation is eta(e,e) = 1 and eta(n,e) = gamma beta, whence h(e,e) = 1 + gamma^2 beta^2 = gamma^2 (1 - beta^2 + beta^2) = gamma^2 by gamma^{-2} = 1 - beta^2 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a), lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a)). (b) The expansion formula is clause (d) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples; the material-metric statements are clauses (b) and (c) of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching applied to e, with theta(e,e) = gamma^2 theta(s,s) because e = |e|_h s = gamma s. The logarithmic rate identity follows from d/dtau = (gamma/c) d/dt and d gamma/dt = gamma^3 beta beta' = gamma^3 q'q''/c^2 (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative). (c) Substituting alpha t = 3c/5 gives beta = 3/5, gamma^{-2} = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25, gamma = 5/4, gamma^2 = 25/16, and theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3 = (125/64)(alpha^2 (3c/(5alpha))/c^3) = (125/64)(3alpha/(5c^2)) = 75alpha/(64c^2), so c theta(s,s) = 75alpha/(64c); the remaining values are substitutions. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.
