before.title: The guided-ring Sagnac delay: return times and receiver proper-time difference for counter-propagating guided signals on a rotating ring
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Fix R > 0, a real Omega with |Omega| R < c, a real x^3_0 and a real phi_0, and put gamma := (1 - Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius R and height x^3_0 about the x^3-axis, with angular velocity Omega, has material worldlines W_{phi_0}(t) := x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 + Omega t), R sin(phi_0 + Omega t), x^3_0), t in R. (i) The ring worldline and the ring congruence. W_{phi_0} is a C^infinity future timelike worldline with four-velocity gamma(R) (1, -(Omega R/c) sin(phi_0+Omega t), (Omega R/c) cos(phi_0+Omega t), 0) = (gamma/c) partial_t|_{varphi}, where varphi := phi - Omega t is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is a flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence n = gamma(r) [partial_0 + (Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1 + x^1 partial_2)] restricted to r = R, and its proper time tau and the chart time t satisfy d tau = dt/gamma, so tau and t differ from each other by the constant factor gamma on this worldline (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (ii) The guided-signal model. Adopt, as an explicit model assumption of an ideal circular guide attached to the ring and of the signal and detector model below, and not as a consequence of the postulates: two ideal signals are emitted at the common emission event W_{phi_0}(0) into the guide, one co-rotating with the ring and one counter-rotating, and in the inertial chart they follow the curves C_+ and C_- given by phi_+(t) = phi_0 + c t/R and phi_-(t) = phi_0 - c t/R with radius R and height x^3_0, i.e. each guided signal has chart angular rate +c/R or -c/R along the guide ('inertial tangential speed c along the guide'); the detector is an ideal clock carried by the ring material point labelled varphi = phi_0. Each of C_+ and C_- is a future null curve of the chart: its tangent has time component c and spatial part of Euclidean length c, so the tangent has eta-norm 0 and positive time component (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). (iii) Return times and differences. C_+ meets the worldline W_{phi_0} exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c - Omega R), k in Z, and C_- exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c + Omega R), k in Z; the smallest positive meeting times are t_1 := 2 pi R/(c - Omega R) > 0 and t_2 := 2 pi R/(c + Omega R) > 0. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events W_{phi_0}(t_1) and W_{phi_0}(t_2), each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2 R^2) > 0 for Omega > 0. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is (t_1 - t_2)/gamma = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). For Omega = 0 (inertial ring) t_1 = t_2 = 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish; for Omega < 0 the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of C_+ and C_- are interchanged. (iv) Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy. The rest lines of the ring congruence are the curves of constant rotating label satisfying dt/dvarphi = Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2); one circuit varphi -> varphi + 2 pi has the chart-time holonomy Delta t_h = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2 and the receiver proper-time holonomy Delta tau_h = Delta t_h/gamma = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/gamma, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for Omega = 0 both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for Omega != 0, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the cylinder r = R is locally integrable and has the nonvanishing global holonomy just computed; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius). (v) Scope. All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of R and Omega are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Direct computation on the cylinder r = R, using the ring congruence data of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c). (i) Substituting phi = phi_0 + Omega t into the cylinder parametrisation and differentiating with thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives, thm-chain-rule and def-derivative gives the displayed tangent; its eta-norm is gamma^2(-1 + Omega^2R^2/c^2) = -1, so it is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), and the four-velocity relation to the congruence field n and the proper-time factor d tau = dt/gamma follow from dx/dtau = c n and def-sr-proper-time with lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization. (ii) Each curve C_+-, t |-> x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 +- c t/R), R sin(phi_0 +- c t/R), x^3_0), has tangent (c, -+ c sin(phi_0 +- ct/R), +- c cos(phi_0 +- ct/R), 0) of eta-norm -c^2 + c^2 = 0 and positive time component, hence is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). (iii) C_+ meets W_{phi_0} exactly when c t/R = Omega t + 2 pi k for an integer k, i.e. t = 2 pi k R/(c - Omega R); since |Omega|R < c the denominator is positive, so the positive solutions are k = 1,2,..., the smallest being t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - Omega R) > 0. Likewise C_- meets W_{phi_0} exactly when -c t/R = Omega t + 2 pi k, i.e. t = 2 pi k R/(c + Omega R) for integer k, with smallest positive solution t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + Omega R). The difference is t_1 - t_2 = 2 pi R[(c + Omega R) - (c - Omega R)]/((c - Omega R)(c + Omega R)) = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2), and multiplication by the constant factor 1/gamma of (i) converts chart time to detector proper time (lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). The special cases Omega = 0 and Omega < 0 are substitutions. (iv) The rest lines and the holonomy are those computed in thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c); the factor-2 relation is the algebraic identity 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 2 (2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2)) and its proper-time counterpart, and the distinction between the nonintegrable ambient rest distribution and the locally integrable cylinder restriction is the statement of that theorem and of thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius (iii). (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before.physical_scope: Conditional kinematic computation in flat classical special relativity for an ideal rigidly rotating circular ring, an adopted ideal circular guide carrying two counter-propagating guided signals with inertial tangential speed c, and an ideal clock detector on the ring. The guide and detector models are explicit idealizations, not consequences of the special-relativistic postulates; the item excludes real optical fibers, refractive and dispersive media, apparatus, finite resolution, interference and wave optics, gravitation and quantum effects, and it makes no measurement, statistical or empirical claim and no claim about sending signals between different material points of the ring.

before.title: Bell's rockets and thread: constant chart-frame separation of equal chart-frame accelerations with nonvanishing longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions for the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let J be an open interval containing 0, let q: J -> R be C^2 with |q'(t)| < c for every t in J, put gamma(t) := (1 - q'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, let L > 0 and a real pair y_0, z_0 be given, and consider the two rocket worldlines x_0(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t), y_0, z_0) and x_L(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + L, y_0, z_0), t in J. Consider also an idealized thread whose material points are labelled by xi in an open interval containing [0,L] and whose element labelled xi moves on the worldline x_xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + xi, y_0, z_0). Then: (a) Kinematics of the rockets. x_0 and x_L are C^2 future timelike worldlines with four-velocity U_xi(t) = gamma(t) (c, q'(t), 0, 0) (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(e)); the two rockets have equal chart-frame velocity q'(t) at every chart time and their chart-frame separation is the constant q(t) + L - q(t) = L, so their chart-frame accelerations q''(t) are equal as well. (b) The translated congruence and its expansion. On the open set covered by the worldlines, n := gamma(t) (1, q'(t)/c, 0, 0) is a smooth future unit timelike field whose flow lines are the worldlines x_xi (which are translated members of one another); it is the translated congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d), whose unit longitudinal rest vector is s := gamma (q'/c, 1, 0, 0) and whose expansion along s is theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (c)); this quantity is nonzero exactly at parameter values with q'(t) q''(t) nonzero, and it changes sign with q'q''. (c) Rest separation versus chart separation. The material field e := partial_xi is the unit chart displacement e = (0,1,0,0); its rest length per unit label is |e|_h = sqrt(h(e,e)) = gamma(t), and the rest separation between the two rockets, measured with the material metric of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching along the flow, is |e|_h L = gamma(t) L. By that lemma the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is c theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^2, so d(gamma L)/dtau = gamma^4 L q' q''/c^2 and, in particular, whenever q'(t) = v at some time, the rest separation at that time equals L/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) > L if v != 0, with minimum L exactly at parameter values with q' = 0. Thus the chart-frame separation L is constant while the rest separation gamma(t) L is not. (d) Material reading of the thread. If a thread attached to the rockets is modelled by material points following the flow lines of n (each thread element moving with the locally coincident rocket), then by lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching its internal longitudinal material metric component is G_11 = gamma(t)^2 and its own rest-length measure between the two endpoint elements grows from L to gamma(t) L; whenever q'(t) != 0 the thread is stretched relative to its initial length by the factor gamma(t) > 1. A conclusion that an actual thread breaks or is under a definite tension requires an elasticity model with a failure or constitutive criterion; no such model is specified here, and no breaking or tension conclusion is drawn from the kinematic computation alone. (e) Contrast with Born rigidity. The Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) is Born rigid, its neighbouring worldlines have constant rest separation, and its proper accelerations c^2/rho are unequal (def-sr-proper-acceleration); conversely the translated congruence has equal chart-frame velocity and acceleration profiles along its members but is not Born rigid wherever q'q'' != 0. Born rigidity of a congruence is therefore not equivalent to equality of the chart-frame accelerations of its members, and constant chart separation of a family of worldlines is not the constancy of their rest separation. (f) Scope. This is a conditional kinematic deduction in flat classical spacetime about the specified worldlines and the specified material reading of the thread; it contains no dynamics, no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about real threads or real rockets. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Direct computation with the translated congruence. (a) Differentiating x_xi with the chain rule gives (c, q'(t), 0, 0) = (c/gamma) gamma(1, q'/c, 0, 0); its eta-norm is c^2/gamma^2 . (-1 + q'^2/c^2) = -c^2, so it is future timelike and the four-velocity is gamma(c, q', 0, 0) (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets); the chart separation is q(t) + L - q(t) = L by construction. (b) The expansion formula is clause (d) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples, which also identifies n, s and the field; the vanishing statement is the product rule for q'q''. (c) With e = (0,1,0,0) one has eta(n,e) = gamma q'/c and h(e,e) = eta(e,e) + eta(n,e)^2 = 1 + gamma^2 q'^2/c^2 = gamma^2 (gamma^{-2} + q'^2/c^2) = gamma^2 (1 - q'^2/c^2 + q'^2/c^2) = gamma^2, so |e|_h = gamma; the rest separation is |e|_h L by linearity of the material metric along the (constant) label direction, and the evolution is the length clause of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching with u = e/|e|_h = s. The chain-rule identity d gamma/dtau = gamma^4 q'q''/c^2 follows from d gamma/dt = gamma^3 q'q''/c^2 and dtau = dt/gamma, and agrees with the expansion form; the evaluation at a time with q' = v is a substitution. (d) The material metric G_11 = h(e,e) = gamma^2 is the thread's own longitudinal metric by lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a), and its growth is clause (b) of that lemma; the elasticity caveat is part of the statement and is not proved, because no elasticity model is available or claimed. (e) The Rindler facts are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) together with def-sr-proper-acceleration (b), and the non-rigidity of the translated congruence is (b) above. (f) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Bell's rockets and thread: constant chart-frame separation of equal chart-frame accelerations with nonvanishing longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence
after.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$ of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $J$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $q:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ with $|q\prime(t)|<c$, set $\beta=q\prime/c$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $L>0$, and fix transverse coordinates $(y_0,z_0)$. The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.
(a) Every member is $C^2$ future timelike: its chart-time tangent is $(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2/\gamma^2<0$. Its common proper-time function is $\tau(t):=\int_0^t\gamma(v)^{-1}dv$, and its proper four-velocity is $U=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2$. All members have equal chart velocity and acceleration, $q\prime,q\prime\prime$, and their chart separation is the constant $L$.
(b) The four-dimensional extension is essential for applying the material-family lemma. Choose open transverse intervals $Y,Z$ containing $y_0,z_0$, put $\sigma:=c\tau$, let $t=t(\sigma)$ be the inverse on $c\tau(J)$, and set
$$\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z):=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z),\qquad(\xi,y,z)\in B:=I\times Y\times Z.$$
This is an injective $C^2$ immersion onto an open set, with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ and $\partial_\sigma\Phi=n(\Phi)$, where $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a $C^1$ future unit field. Apply the first-order definitions in [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]], which agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] when smooth. The longitudinal unit rest vector is $s_\parallel:=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and
$$\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3.$$
This agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d), is nonzero exactly where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$, and changes sign with that product. When $q$ is smooth the full original smooth-congruence branch is recovered. Restricting the extension to fixed $y_0,z_0$ gives the prescribed thread.
(c) For its material label tangent $e=\partial_\xi\Phi=(0,1,0,0)$, $h(e,e)=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)/\gamma=s_\parallel$. The vector $e/\gamma$ generally is not $s_\parallel$, but horizontality implies $\theta(e/\gamma,e/\gamma)=\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)$. The internal longitudinal material metric is $G_{11}=\gamma^2$, so its length at common flow parameter is
$$\mathcal L(t):=\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}d\xi=\gamma(t)L.$$
It is an internal material metric length, not automatically the finite endpoint distance on one observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane. The local evolution is
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}\log\mathcal L=c\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2,\qquad\frac{d\mathcal L}{d\tau}=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2.$$
At a time with $q\prime=v$, $\mathcal L=L/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\ge L$, with equality exactly for $v=0$. Chart separation stays $L$; the material length is constant precisely when $q\prime{}^2$ is constant, and has nonzero local rate wherever $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$.
(d) Under the stipulated material reading that thread elements follow these flow lines, the initial internal length is $\gamma(0)L$ and its relative factor is $\gamma(t)/\gamma(0)$. Relative to that initial state it stretches where $\gamma(t)>\gamma(0)$, shrinks where $\gamma(t)<\gamma(0)$, and has equal length where the factors agree. In the special initially resting case $q\prime(0)=0$, the initial length is $L$ and every state with $q\prime(t)\ne0$ has stretch factor $\gamma(t)>1$. No elasticity or failure criterion is supplied, so neither breaking nor a definite tension of an actual thread follows.
(e) The Rindler congruence in [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](b) is Born rigid, with constant internal rest separations and unequal proper accelerations $c^2/\rho$ at distinct radial labels ([[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]). Equal chart-velocity and acceleration profiles in the translated family do not imply Born rigidity where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$. Constant chart separation and constant internal rest metric are distinct kinematic conditions.
(f) This is a conditional flat-spacetime deduction for prescribed worldlines and the stated material reading. It assumes no dynamical or elastic model, force law, material failure criterion, measurement or empirical fact, and asserts nothing about real threads or rockets. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy:
(a) Differentiate the given worldlines. The chart-time tangent has norm $-c^2+q\prime{}^2=-c^2/\gamma^2$ and positive time component, so it is nonzero future timelike. Proper time gives $d\tau/dt=1/\gamma$ and $U=dx/d\tau=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$; its norm is $-c^2$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). The separation and equality of chart derivatives follow directly.
(b) Since $q$ is $C^2$, $\gamma$ is $C^1$ and $\tau\prime=1/\gamma$ is positive $C^1$, so $\tau$ is $C^2$ and strictly increasing. [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] gives its $C^1$ inverse; its derivative $dt/d\tau=\gamma(t(\tau))$ is $C^1$, hence the inverse is $C^2$. Scaling to $\sigma=c\tau$ gives $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$. Thus $\Phi$ is $C^2$, its four derivative columns are $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$, and its determinant in the chart is $\gamma>0$. Its inverse is explicit from $t=x^0/c$, $\xi=x^1-q(t)$, $y=x^2,z=x^3$, so it is injective with open image and satisfies the precise $J\times B\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ family hypothesis of [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]. The $C^1$ field $n$ depends only on $t=x^0/c$. Using the first-order projected formula for $\theta$, and the fact that $s_\parallel$ is horizontal, Writing $\dot\beta=d\beta/dt$, the only nonzero coordinate derivatives are $\partial_0n_0=-\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$ and $\partial_0n_1=\gamma^3\dot\beta/c$. Therefore $s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$, giving $\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3$. This proves the formula with exactly $C^2$ data and agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d); it does not require a smooth-only supplier for the nonsmooth branch.
(c) Compute $h(e,e)=1+\gamma^2\beta^2=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)=e+\gamma\beta n=\gamma s_\parallel$. Since $\theta(n,\cdot)=0$, the difference of $e/\gamma$ and $s_\parallel$ is annihilated by $\theta$. Applying [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] to the four-dimensional family, then restricting to fixed transverse labels, gives $G=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^2,1,1)$ and the length/rate identities. Independently $d\gamma/dt=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$ and $d/d\tau=\gamma d/dt$ give $d(\gamma L)/d\tau=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$. The derivative with respect to geometric proper length is instead $d/d\sigma=(\gamma/c)d/dt$. The length $\gamma L$ is exactly the integral of the pulled-back local rest metric over the fixed-label segment; the fixed-$\sigma$ segment need not lie in an endpoint observer's orthogonal hyperplane. The equality/constancy statements follow from $\gamma=(1-q\prime{}^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
(d) Compare $\mathcal L(t)$ with $\mathcal L(0)=\gamma(0)L$. This gives the factor and the stretch/shrink cases without an initial-rest hypothesis. Specializing $q\prime(0)=0$ gives the original initially resting stretch conclusion. Material failure and constitutive stress require an additional model and are not deduced.
(e) Apply the exact smooth Rindler clause of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] and [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]; its rigidity and unequal radial accelerations provide the stated contrast. (f) Retain all physical qualifications and the absence of empirical or material-dynamics conclusions.

before.title: Guided-ring Sagnac delay worked at angular velocity Omega R = 3c/5
before.statement: Worked instance of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. Let R > 0 and Omega = 3c/(5R), so that Omega R = 3c/5, |Omega|R < c and gamma = (1 - 9/25)^{-1/2} = 5/4. Work in the inertial chart with x^0 = c t and let the ring have its plane x^3 = 0 and let the emission event be E = x^{-1}(0, R, 0, 0), where the material point labelled varphi = 0 has phi_0 = 0. (a) Return times. The co-rotating guided signal has phi_+(t) = c t/R and the emitting material point has phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the signal meets that point when c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi, i.e. t_1 = 5 pi R/c (the relative angular rate is 8c/(5R)); the counter-rotating signal C_-, phi_-(t) = -c t/R, meets it when -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi, i.e. t_2 = 5 pi R/(4c). The reception events are e_1 = x^{-1}(5 pi R, R cos(3 pi), R sin(3 pi), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R, -R, 0, 0) and e_2 = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, R cos(3 pi/4), R sin(3 pi/4), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, -R/sqrt(2), R/sqrt(2), 0), where the angle values use the parity, addition and Pythagorean identities for sine and cosine (def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero, thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas, cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity). (b) Differences and the factor-2 holonomy check. The chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 5 pi R/c - 5 pi R/(4c) = 15 pi R/(4c) = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2), and the detector proper-time difference is (t_1-t_2)·(4/5) = 3 pi R/c = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). The ring rest-line chart-time holonomy of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (iv) is Delta t_h = 15 pi R/(8c), exactly half of t_1 - t_2, and the corresponding receiver proper-time holonomy is (4/5)·15 pi R/(8c) = 3 pi R/(2c), exactly half of 3 pi R/c; this verifies the factor-2 relation of that clause. The ambient rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable while the cylinder-restricted one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with the nonzero global holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c)). (c) Inertial limit. For Omega = 0 with the same R the two return times are both 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with the adopted ideal circular guide, ideal signals and the ideal clock detector of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (ii); no interference phase, apparatus, medium, measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made, and the idealizations of that theorem are retained.
before.strategy: Substitute Omega = 3c/(5R) into the exact formulas of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. (a) The angle of the material point is phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the co-rotating guided signal has angle c t/R, so the reunion condition is c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi k, with smallest positive solution k = 1, i.e. t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - 3c/5) = 5 pi R/c; the counter-rotating signal has angle -c t/R, so the condition is -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi k, i.e. t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + 3c/5) = 5 pi R/(4c). The reception events are obtained by substituting these times into the parametrisation of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (i), with the elementary sine and cosine values cos(3 pi) = -1, sin(3 pi) = 0 and cos(3 pi/4) = -sin(3 pi/4) = -1/sqrt(2) supplied by the parity, addition and Pythagorean identities. (b) The differences are the substitutions into 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 4 pi (3c/(5R))R^2/(c^2(1-9/25)) = 15 pi R/(4c) and into (t_1-t_2)/gamma with 1/gamma = 4/5; the holonomy Delta t_h = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) evaluates to 2 pi (3c/(5R))R^2/(c^2(16/25)) = 15 pi R/(8c), half of 15 pi R/(4c), and its proper-time counterpart is (4/5)·15 pi R/(8c) = 3 pi R/(2c), half of 3 pi R/c. The nonintegrability statements are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c). (c) is the Omega = 0 substitution. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Wikipedia, 'Sagnac effect': the basic circular case with t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - R omega) and t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + R omega), used with the exact rational velocity ratio 3/5

B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages): Sections 8.1.1-8.1.3 pp. 165-166 (the closed-circuit synchronization discrepancy and the Sagnac effect of a rotating ring); signature (+---) converted to (-+++), c = 1 formulas restored to x^0 = c t

before.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
before.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted action on compactly supported variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.
before.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation (the schema records postulates with formulation, scope and sources, not a deduction). The mathematical content used in the formulation is confined to the model equations and the displayed tensors; conservation is deliberately NOT part of this postulate. Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed.

before.physical_scope: Classical continuum matter in flat affine Minkowski spacetime: a real scalar field with potential, dust and a perfect fluid, with the stated evolution equations adopted as model premises. Excludes gravity, electromagnetic coupling, general relativity, thermodynamics and equations of state, viscosity, dissipation and heat conduction, quantum or statistical matter, and every empirical or measurement claim; the models are adopted, not derived from experiment.

after.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
after.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted local action density, with stationarity defined by the finite relative action for compactly supported field variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). (v) Adopted observer readings and units. For a tensor physically assigned to matter in this model, all inertial components $T^{ab}$ have units joule per cubic metre. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, an ideal observer with future unit direction $n$ and four-velocity $U=cn$ reads the numerical contractions of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] as energy density $\varepsilon_n=T^{ab}n_an_b$, momentum density $\pi_n^a=-c^{-1}h^a{}_bT^{bc}n_c$ and rest stress $S_n^{ab}=h^a{}_ch^b{}_dT^{cd}$. Here $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$. In an adapted inertial frame these are $T^{00}$, $T^{0i}/c$ and $T^{ij}$ respectively, and the energy-flux components are $cT^{i0}=c^2\pi_n^i$. Momentum density has units kilogram per square metre per second; energy flux has units watt per square metre; rest stress has units joule per cubic metre. These identifications are adopted model readings, not mathematical facts about an arbitrary symmetric tensor and not reported measurements. If $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ is assigned to external exchange, the spatial components $f^i$ are force per volume and $cf^0$ is power per volume: the corresponding numerical balances are $\partial_t(T^{00})+\partial_i(cT^{i0})=cf^0$ and $\partial_t(T^{0j}/c)+\partial_iT^{ij}=f^j$. Neither assignment selects a force law or asserts conservation. This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.

Sources: the scalar action and equation of motion are 4.5.1 of Tong; the fluid equations are 4.5.4 of Tong and the displayed tensors are (4.53) of Tong, (1.106)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.3-9.2.6 of Crowell; the choice to adopt, rather than derive, the matter dynamics follows the source statements that conservation follows from each model's own equations of motion (Carroll p. 30) and that matter actions and equations of state are separate model assumptions (Tong 4.5). No empirical support is claimed. The observer component reading removed from mathematical definitions/lemmas is explicitly adopted in(v), including the exact c factors: $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ turns the tensor balance into the two displayed SI balances, while the observer-decomposition lemma provides only the numerical contractions/components. This is preservation of the framework's stated interpretation, not a new empirical law or a deduction of an observer measurement. Local relative actions, not a possibly divergent background integral over all Omega, formulate(i).

before.title: Specified low-speed momentum-energy correspondence between the relativistic measured quantities and the Newtonian comparison quantities
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("pthm specified p/E correspondence"; closure "baseline M08; Q4 controlled correspondence"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08
before.design_state: complete conditional deduction of the uniform correspondence from the adopted momentum/measurement postulate and the pair's uniform expansion lemma; constants depend on the speed bound
before.physical_scope: Flat special-relativity massive classical particles (constant mass m>0, P=mU) with the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified as E_n, q_n, T_n by post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics, in inertial frames and in the bounded low-speed domain |w|^2 <= z_0 c^2 with z_0<1, in the SI conventions. The error bounds are uniform on that domain and depend on z_0; nothing is asserted uniformly as |w| -> c. Excludes massless particles, variable mass, forces, interactions and interactions mechanisms, accelerated observers, gravity, quantum and statistical descriptions, and every empirical claim, measurement value or precision statement.
before.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] (massive-particle momentum, the identification of measured quantities and isolated collision balance) and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$, spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and inertial chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$ and four-momentum $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $y$ be a worldline of the particle whose inertial coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ and whose coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)\in S$ of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]\,(b) equals a fixed $w$ at the instant considered; then in this frame $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

Fix $z_0\in[0,1)$ and suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ be the Newtonian comparison quantities of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. With $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$ the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified in clause (ii) of the adopted postulate, $m(P)$ the invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and $R_E,R_q$ the remainders of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]:

(a) [Energy] $E_n(P)=mc^2+N_K(m,w)+R_E$ and $E_n(P)-T_n(P)=mc^2$; $|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2$. So the measured energy of the moving particle exceeds its rest energy by the Newtonian kinetic energy up to the displayed uniform bound of order $m|w|^4/c^2$.

(b) [Kinetic energy] $T_n(P)=N_K(m,w)+R_E$, hence $|T_n(P)-N_K(m,w)|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,N_K(m,w)$: the relative deviation from the Newtonian kinetic energy is at most $2K(z_0)z$.

(c) [Momentum] $q_n(P)=N_p(m,w)+R_q$, and $|R_q|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|N_p(m,w)|$; for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian momentum is at most $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)z$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $w=q_n(P)/(m\gamma_w)$ exactly, and $|w-q_n(P)/m|=(\gamma_w-1)|w|/\gamma_w\le(\gamma_w-1)|w|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|w|$; at $z=0$ one has $w=0$, $q_n(P)=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$ and $T_n(P)=0$, and $m(P)=m$ always.

(e) [Scope and uniformity] The constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all masses $m>0$, all states, instants and inertial frames with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. The statement is a conditional correspondence between the model's adopted measured quantities and the comparison functionals of a named frame: it identifies no framework with another, asserts no convergence of trajectories, forces or interactions and no limit in which the constant $c$ varies, gives no bound uniform in $|w|<c$ (see [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]]) and makes no empirical claim.
before.strategy:
The deduction is the transport of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]] through the adopted identification of measured quantities. By clause (ii) of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy of the particle are $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$, and by clause (i) the particle's four-momentum is $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant; the SI units of the comparison functionals and of $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The frame data identify the state's relative velocity with the coordinate velocity: clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] states that for the frame's stationary observer $n=e_0$ the relative velocity of clause (d) is the coordinate velocity $w$, and clause (b) of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] gives the components $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.

Under the hypothesis $z=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, the batch lemma gives $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$, $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with the displayed bounds, and $R_E,R_q$ depend on the state only through $z$, $m$, $|w|$ and the constants $K(z_0)$; clause (a) is exactly this substitution together with the definition $T_n=E_n-mc^2$ and the postulate's identification of $mc^2$ as the rest energy, clause (b) divides the bound by $N_K=\tfrac12m|w|^2$, clause (c) divides by $|N_p|=m|w|$, and clause (d) uses $q_n=m\gamma_ww$ so that $w-q_n/m=w(1-1/\gamma_w)=w(\gamma_w-1)/\gamma_w$ with $|\gamma_w-1|$ bounded as in the Taylor lemma. Clause (e) records that no step used more than $z\le z_0$, and that no claim beyond the stated class follows: the bounds are conditional, and the failure of any speed-independent constant is exhibited in [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]] and on the companion example page.

after.title: Specified low-speed momentum-energy correspondence between the relativistic measured quantities and the Newtonian comparison quantities
after.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("pthm specified p/E correspondence"; closure "baseline M08; Q4 controlled correspondence"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08
after.design_state: complete conditional deduction of the uniform correspondence from the adopted momentum/measurement postulate and the pair's uniform expansion lemma; constants depend on the speed bound
after.physical_scope: Flat special-relativity massive classical particles (constant mass m>0, P=mU) with the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified as E_n, q_n, T_n by post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics, in inertial frames and in the bounded low-speed domain |w|^2 <= z_0 c^2 with z_0<1, in the SI conventions. The error bounds are uniform on that domain and depend on z_0; nothing is asserted uniformly as |w| -> c. Excludes massless particles, variable mass, forces, interactions and interactions mechanisms, accelerated observers, gravity, quantum and statistical descriptions, and every empirical claim, measurement value or precision statement.
after.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] (massive-particle momentum, the identification of measured quantities and isolated collision balance) and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$, spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and inertial chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$ and four-momentum $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $y$ be a worldline of the particle whose inertial coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ and whose coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)\in S$ of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]\,(b) equals a fixed $w$ at the instant considered; then in this frame $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

Fix $z_0\in[0,1)$ and suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ be the Newtonian comparison quantities of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. With $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$ the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified in clause (ii) of the adopted postulate, $m(P)$ the invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and $R_E,R_q$ the remainders of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]:

(a) [Energy] $E_n(P)=mc^2+N_K(m,w)+R_E$ and $E_n(P)-T_n(P)=mc^2$; $|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2$. So the measured energy of the moving particle exceeds its rest energy by the Newtonian kinetic energy up to the displayed uniform bound of order $m|w|^4/c^2$.

(b) [Kinetic energy] $T_n(P)=N_K(m,w)+R_E$, hence $|T_n(P)-N_K(m,w)|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,N_K(m,w)$: for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian kinetic energy is at most $2K(z_0)z$.

(c) [Momentum] $q_n(P)=N_p(m,w)+R_q$, and $|R_q|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|N_p(m,w)|$; for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian momentum is at most $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)z$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $w=q_n(P)/(m\gamma_w)$ exactly, and $|w-q_n(P)/m|=(\gamma_w-1)|w|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|w|$; at $z=0$ one has $w=0$, $q_n(P)=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$ and $T_n(P)=0$, and $m(P)=m$ always.

(e) [Scope and uniformity] The constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all masses $m>0$, all states, instants and inertial frames with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. The statement is a conditional correspondence between the model's adopted measured quantities and the comparison functionals of a named frame: it identifies no framework with another, asserts no convergence of trajectories, forces or interactions and no limit in which the constant $c$ varies, gives no bound uniform in $|w|<c$ (see [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]]) and makes no empirical claim.

before.title: The Rindler chart: causal horizons of a uniformly accelerated observer and the restrictions of radar time and distance
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and let W := {x^1 > |x^0|} be the right wedge. Let Phi and n be the Rindler chart and congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b): Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 with inverse rho = sqrt((x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0)), pullback metric -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, and acceleration field a_cg = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho. Fix rho_0 > 0 and real y_0,z_0, and let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0, y = y_0, z = z_0, parametrized by its proper time tau with theta = c tau/rho_0; by def-sr-proper-acceleration its proper acceleration is c^2/rho_0. Write U(q) := q^0 + q^1 and V(q) := q^0 - q^1 for events q, so that U = rho e^{theta} and V = -rho e^{-theta} on W, and write <= and J^+, J^- for the causal reachability relations of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Chart domain and light rays. Phi is a smooth bijection of R x (0,inf) x R^2 onto W with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly W and the set rho = 0, i.e. the union of the null planes {x^1 = x^0} and {x^1 = -x^0}, is not part of the chart. Along the worldline rho = rho_0 one has V = -rho_0 e^{-theta} -> 0^- and U -> +infinity as theta -> +infinity, while U = rho_0 e^{theta} -> 0^+ and V -> -infinity as theta -> -infinity. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0 and meet O are exactly the lines of constant V (on which dtheta = +drho/rho) and the lines of constant U (on which dtheta = -drho/rho). (ii) Causal horizons. An event q satisfies q <= p for some event p of O if and only if V(q) < 0; an event q satisfies p <= q for some event p of O if and only if U(q) > 0. Consequently no event with V(q) >= 0 can ever influence O; this set contains the null plane {x^1 = x^0}, the left wedge {x^1 < -|x^0|} and the future wedge {x^0 > |x^1|}; and no event with U(q) <= 0 can ever be influenced by O, a set containing the null plane {x^1 = -x^0}, the left wedge and the past wedge {x^0 < -|x^1|}. The null plane {x^1 = x^0} is the boundary of the causal past of O (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as theta -> +infinity), and the null plane {x^1 = -x^0} is the boundary of the causal future of O (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to O in both directions. The same criteria with O any other congruence worldline rho = rho_1, y = y_1, z = z_1 hold verbatim: the constants rho_0, y_0, z_0 do not enter. (iii) Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector. Fix rho_m > 0 with rho_m != rho_0 and let R_m be the congruence worldline rho = rho_m, y = y_0, z = z_0 (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with O, with proper acceleration c^2/rho_m). Let e_- be the event of O at parameter theta_e (so tau(e_-) = rho_0 theta_e/c up to the base point of tau), let q_m be the event of R_m lying on the future null straight line from e_- in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0, and let e_+ be the event of O lying on the future null straight line from q_m; the reflection at q_m is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving R_m's motion unchanged, as in def-sr-operational-radar-protocol. Then e_-, q_m, e_+ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of q_m is theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|, the return event satisfies theta(e_+) = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| and (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = theta_m, so the round trip lasts 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in Rindler time and (2rho_0/c)|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in O's proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to q_m the radar time tau_rad(q_m) = (rho_0/c) theta_m plus the base constant of tau and the radar distance rho_rad(q_m) = rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)|; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices theta = const, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice theta = theta_m the two worldlines are at rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|, whereas for rho_m = 2rho_0 the radar distance is rho_0 log 2 < rho_0, because log is strictly increasing and e > 2 implies log 2 < log e = 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws); the two notions agree only for rho_m = rho_0. As rho_m -> 0^+ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration c^2/rho_m diverges; as rho_m -> +infinity the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to 0. (iv) Restrictions of the protocol. No event with V >= 0 - in particular no event of the horizon plane {x^1 = x^0}, of the left wedge or of the future wedge - can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from O, because by (ii) no event of O can causally precede it in the required emission-reflection-reception configuration; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit rho_m -> 0^+. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of A. (v) Scope. All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Instantiate the causality lemmas of the causal model in the Rindler chart. (i) The chart assertions are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), together with the identities U = rho e^{theta}, V = -rho e^{-theta}: on a line of constant V one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta - theta_0}, so dtheta = drho/rho and ds^2 = -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 = 0 exactly, and the tangent with increasing theta has positive time component, so the line is future null; on a line of constant U one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_0 - theta} and dtheta = -drho/rho, and again ds^2 = 0 with a future tangent (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light). The limits along rho = rho_0 use the defining exponentials. (ii) By lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion (c), q <= p(theta) is equivalent to A(theta) >= sqrt(B(theta)^2 + r^2) with A(theta) := rho_0 sinh theta - q^0, B(theta) := rho_0 cosh theta - q^1 and r^2 := (q^2-y_0)^2 + (q^3-z_0)^2. For the direct implication assume V(q) = q^0 - q^1 < 0; then A^2 - B^2 - r^2 = -rho_0^2 + 2rho_0(q^1 cosh theta - q^0 sinh theta) + ((q^0)^2 - (q^1)^2 - r^2), and q^1 cosh theta - q^0 sinh theta = (1/2)(q^1 - q^0)e^{theta} + (1/2)(q^1 + q^0)e^{-theta} tends to +infinity as theta -> +infinity because the coefficient (1/2)(q^1-q^0) = -(1/2)V(q) of e^{theta} is positive (thm-exponential-addition-formula, thm-exponential-limits-and-range); since A(theta) -> +infinity too, both inequalities hold for all sufficiently large theta, so q <= p(theta) for such theta. For the reverse implication, if p(theta) - q is future causal then its time component dominates its first spatial component, so 0 <= (p(theta)-q)^0 - (p(theta)-q)^1 = V(p(theta)) - V(q) = -rho_0 e^{-theta} - V(q), i.e. V(q) <= -rho_0 e^{-theta} < 0. The statement for U is the same computation with the signs of the first spatial component reversed, using U(p(theta)) = rho_0 e^{theta} > 0: p(theta) <= q implies U(q) >= rho_0 e^{theta} > 0, and conversely U(q) > 0 forces the two inequalities for theta -> -infinity (where q^1 cosh theta - q^0 sinh theta = -(1/2)V(q)e^{theta} + (1/2)U(q)e^{-theta} -> +infinity because the coefficient of e^{-theta} is (1/2)U(q) > 0, and (q - p(theta))^0 -> +infinity). The set inclusions are evaluations: on the left wedge and on the future wedge V >= 0, on the left wedge and on the past wedge U <= 0, the plane {x^1 = x^0} is V = 0 and the plane {x^1 = -x^0} is U = 0. The reading of 'influence' as signal transmission is post-sr-causal-signal-propagation (i)-(ii). The independence of the constants rho_0,y_0,z_0 is plain from the two criteria. (iii) The null line of constant V through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta-theta_e}, which is increasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_m/rho_0) when rho_m > rho_0. The null line of constant U through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_e-theta}, decreasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_0/rho_m) when rho_m < rho_0. In both cases the displacement from e_- to q_m is a positive multiple of (1,1,0,0) or (1,-1,0,0), hence future null, and theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|. From q_m the return line is the other null family: it reaches rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = theta_m + |log(rho_m/rho_0)| = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)|, again along a future null displacement, and uniqueness holds because through a point of the plane there passes exactly one future null line of each family and a fixed congruence worldline is met by such a line in exactly one event. The proper time of O between the two events is rho_0 (theta(e_+) - theta_e)/c by def-sr-proper-time and lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization applied to the unit-tangent flow line; def-sr-operational-radar-protocol converts the round trip into radar time (tau(e_-)+tau(e_+))/2 and radar distance c(tau(e_+)-tau(e_-))/2, giving the displayed values. The comparison with the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) and def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance; the numerical case rho_m = 2rho_0 uses log 2 < 1, which follows from e > 2, log e = 1 and strict increase of log (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). The limits as rho_m -> 0^+ and rho_m -> +infinity follow from |log| -> +infinity and from c^2/rho_m. (iv) The protocol requires the three events; by (ii) an event with V >= 0 is in the causal future of no event of O (nor in the causal past in the required reflection configuration), so the emission-reflection-reception triple does not exist. (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

Fix rho_0 > 0 and real y_0,z_0, and let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0, y = y_0, z = z_0, parametrized by its proper time tau with theta = c tau/rho_0; by def-sr-proper-acceleration its proper acceleration is c^2/rho_0. Write U(q) := q^0 + q^1 and V(q) := q^0 - q^1 for events q, so that U = rho e^{theta} and V = -rho e^{-theta} on W, and write <= and J^+, J^- for the causal reachability relations of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Chart domain and light rays. Phi is a smooth bijection of R x (0,inf) x R^2 onto W with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly W and rho = 0 is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of W in the affine model is {x^1 = |x^0|}, with arbitrary x^2,x^3: it is the union of the two null half-planes {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} and {x^1 = -x^0 >= 0}. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline rho = rho_0 one has V = -rho_0 e^{-theta} -> 0^- and U -> +infinity as theta -> +infinity, while U = rho_0 e^{theta} -> 0^+ and V -> -infinity as theta -> -infinity. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0 and meet O are exactly the lines of constant V (on which dtheta = +drho/rho) and the lines of constant U (on which dtheta = -drho/rho). (ii) Causal horizons. An event q satisfies q <= p for some event p of O if and only if V(q) < 0; an event q satisfies p <= q for some event p of O if and only if U(q) > 0. Consequently no event with V(q) >= 0 can ever influence O; this set contains the null plane {x^1 = x^0}, the left wedge {x^1 < -|x^0|} and the future wedge {x^0 > |x^1|}; and no event with U(q) <= 0 can ever be influenced by O, a set containing the null plane {x^1 = -x^0}, the left wedge and the past wedge {x^0 < -|x^1|}. The null plane {x^1 = x^0} is the boundary of the causal past of O (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as theta -> +infinity), and the null plane {x^1 = -x^0} is the boundary of the causal future of O (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to O in both directions. The same criteria with O any other congruence worldline rho = rho_1, y = y_1, z = z_1 hold verbatim: the constants rho_0, y_0, z_0 do not enter. (iii) Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector. Fix rho_m > 0 with rho_m != rho_0 and let R_m be the congruence worldline rho = rho_m, y = y_0, z = z_0 (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with O, with proper acceleration c^2/rho_m). Let e_- be the event of O at parameter theta_e (so tau(e_-) = rho_0 theta_e/c up to the base point of tau), let q_m be the event of R_m lying on the future null straight line from e_- in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0, and let e_+ be the event of O lying on the future null straight line from q_m; the reflection at q_m is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving R_m's motion unchanged, as in def-sr-operational-radar-protocol. Then e_-, q_m, e_+ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of q_m is theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|, the return event satisfies theta(e_+) = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| and (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = theta_m, so the round trip lasts 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in Rindler time and (2rho_0/c)|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in O's proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to q_m the radar time tau_rad(q_m) = (rho_0/c) theta_m plus the base constant of tau and the radar distance rho_rad(q_m) = rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)|; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices theta = const, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice theta = theta_m the two worldlines are at rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|, whereas for rho_m = 2rho_0 the radar distance is rho_0 log 2 < rho_0, because log is strictly increasing and e > 2 implies log 2 < log e = 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws); For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r=\rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r<r-1$ when $r>1$ and $-\log r>1-r$ when $0<r<1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r=1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As rho_m -> 0^+ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration c^2/rho_m diverges; as rho_m -> +infinity the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to 0. (iv) Restrictions of the protocol. No event with V >= 0 - in particular no event of the horizon plane {x^1 = x^0}, of the left wedge or of the future wedge - can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from O, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on O: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with U <= 0 lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from O. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy U > 0 and V < 0, equivalently it must belong to W; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit rho_m -> 0^+. For example q = x^{-1}(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has U(q)=V(q)=2rho_0>0. It is causally after O at theta=0, since the displacement is (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0), future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from O at theta=log 2, with displacement (5rho_0/4,-5rho_0/4,0,0). Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to O, so receives no radar assignment from O. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of A. (v) Scope. All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Instantiate the causality lemmas of the causal model in the Rindler chart. (i) The chart assertions are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), together with the identities U = rho e^{theta}, V = -rho e^{-theta}: on a line of constant V one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta - theta_0}, so dtheta = drho/rho and ds^2 = -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 = 0 exactly, and the tangent with increasing theta has positive time component, so the line is future null; on a line of constant U one has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_0 - theta} and dtheta = -drho/rho, and again ds^2 = 0 with a future tangent (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light). The limits along rho = rho_0 use the defining exponentials. The wedge boundary follows from the continuous inequality x1>|x0|: its closure is x1>=|x0|, since a boundary point is approached by increasing x1 by a positive amount. Thus the boundary is x1=|x0|, comprising only the indicated half-planes; at fixed finite theta, rho tending to zero does not parametrize the entire boundary. (ii) Write p(theta)=(rho_0 sinh theta,rho_0 cosh theta,y_0,z_0), Up=rho_0 e^theta, Vp=-rho_0 e^(-theta), and r^2=(q^2-y_0)^2+(q^3-z_0)^2. For a displacement D, the future causal coordinate criterion is equivalent to DeltaU>=0, DeltaV>=0 and DeltaU DeltaV>=r^2: D0=(DeltaU+DeltaV)/2, D1=(DeltaU-DeltaV)/2 and D0^2-D1^2=DeltaU DeltaV. For q<=p, necessity gives Vp-Vq>=0, hence Vq<=Vp<0. Conversely if Vq<0, as theta tends to +infinity the difference Vp-Vq tends to the positive number -Vq and Up-Uq tends to +infinity. Therefore both differences are positive and their product exceeds the fixed r^2 for sufficiently large theta; the coordinate criterion proves q<=p. For p<=q, necessity gives Uq-Up>=0, hence Uq>=Up>0. Conversely if Uq>0, as theta tends to -infinity the difference Uq-Up tends to the positive number Uq and Vq-Vp tends to +infinity; again their product eventually exceeds r^2 and p<=q follows. These complete arguments include arbitrary transverse positions. The full planes V=0 and U=0 are respectively the boundaries of these open causal unions; direct coordinate signs give the left/future/past wedge inclusions. The signal reading is conditional on post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the criteria do not depend on rho_0,y_0,z_0. (iii) The null line of constant V through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta-theta_e}, which is increasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_m/rho_0) when rho_m > rho_0. The null line of constant U through e_- has rho = rho_0 e^{theta_e-theta}, decreasing in theta; it meets rho = rho_m at theta_m = theta_e + log(rho_0/rho_m) when rho_m < rho_0. In both cases the displacement from e_- to q_m is a positive multiple of (1,1,0,0) or (1,-1,0,0), hence future null, and theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|. From q_m the return line is the other null family: it reaches rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = theta_m + |log(rho_m/rho_0)| = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)|, again along a future null displacement, and uniqueness holds because through a point of the plane there passes exactly one future null line of each family and a fixed congruence worldline is met by such a line in exactly one event. The proper time of O between the two events is rho_0 (theta(e_+) - theta_e)/c by def-sr-proper-time and lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization applied to the unit-tangent flow line; def-sr-operational-radar-protocol converts the round trip into radar time (tau(e_-)+tau(e_+))/2 and radar distance c(tau(e_+)-tau(e_-))/2, giving the displayed values. The comparison with the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) and def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance; the numerical case rho_m = 2rho_0 uses log 2 < 1, which follows from e > 2, log e = 1 and strict increase of log (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). For the full equality classification, put $r=\rho_m/\rho_0>0$. By thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral, log is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with derivative $1/u$, and therefore continuous there by cor-differentiable-implies-continuous. If $r>1$, cor-mean-value-theorem on $[1,r]$ gives $\xi\in(1,r)$ with $\log r=(r-1)/\xi<r-1$. If $0<r<1$, the same theorem on $[r,1]$ gives $\xi\in(r,1)$ with $-\log r=(1-r)/\xi>1-r$. Multiplying by $\rho_0>0$ proves radar distance strictly smaller than rest distance for an outer reflector and strictly larger for an inner reflector. Only $r=1$ gives zero in both formulas. Their continuity at $r=1$ follows from continuity of log and absolute value; this is the degenerate formula extension, not an assertion that a zero-length null leg satisfies the distinct-reflector protocol. The limits as rho_m -> 0^+ and rho_m -> +infinity follow from |log| -> +infinity and from c^2/rho_m. (iv) A radar triple requires e_-<=q and q<=e_+ with e_-,e_+ on O, indeed both displacements null in the protocol. By (ii), Vq>=0 makes q<=e_+ impossible, while Uq<=0 makes e_-<=q impossible. This is a return obstruction in the former case and an emission obstruction in the latter; both are needed for the round trip. The displayed q=(2rho_0,0,y_0,z_0) has future timelike displacement (2rho_0,-rho_0,0,0) from O(0), norm -3rho_0^2<0. O(log2) has coordinates (3rho_0/4,5rho_0/4,y_0,z_0), yielding the displayed future null displacement to q. Since Vq=2rho_0>0 no causal return to O exists. The infinite radar distance as rho_m decreases to zero is the logarithmic limit in (iii), not a spacetime singularity. (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The Rindler horizon is a chart boundary, not a boundary or singularity of the spacetime
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'In the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the inertial chart x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3), the null plane H := {x^1 = x^0}, which is the boundary of the Rindler wedge W = {x^1 > |x^0|} of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), is a boundary of the model in the following three senses: (i) no future causal curve crosses from {x^1 > x^0} to {x^1 < x^0}; (ii) H separates all causal relations, so no event of {x^1 > x^0} is causally related to any event of {x^1 < x^0}; and (iii) the metric degenerates on H, so that H is a singular boundary of the spacetime on which the model fails.' Counterexample: (a) A future timelike segment crossing H and separating causal relations fails. Let p := x^{-1}(-1,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(3,1,0,0), and let y: [0,1] -> A be the affine segment y(s) := p + s(q-p). The displacement q - p has chart components (4,1,0,0), so eta(q-p,q-p) = -16 + 1 < 0 and the time component is 4 > 0: the segment is a future timelike curve (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Its coordinate function x^0 - x^1 takes the values -1 at s = 0 and +2 at s = 1, hence vanishes at s = 1/3: a future timelike curve crosses H, refuting (i). Moreover q is in the causal future of p in the sense p <= q of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space, and p and q lie on opposite sides of H, so the segment relates events on opposite sides, refuting (ii). (b) Events of H and of its complement are causally related in both directions. The event r := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) satisfies r <= x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) because the displacement (1,1,0,0) is future null; and x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) < x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) because the displacement (1,1/2,0,0) satisfies -1 + 1/4 < 0 with positive time component (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion (c)). The event x^{-1}(1,1,0,0) lies on H while r and x^{-1}(2,3/2,0,0) do not, so H neither separates causal relations nor consists of causally isolated events. (c) No metric degeneracy occurs. In the inertial chart the matrix of eta is the constant diag(-1,1,1,1) on the whole model, hence eta is nondegenerate and constant everywhere, in particular on H; and x^{-1}(1,1,0,0), an event of H, is the midpoint of the future timelike segment of (a) on which the metric is the ordinary flat metric. The Rindler map Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) with theta in R and rho > 0 is, by thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), a smooth bijection onto W with a smooth inverse; its domain simply satisfies rho > 0, so the set rho = 0 and hence H are outside the chart domain, and the failure of the map to be defined there is a property of the coordinate map, not of eta. (d) An inertial worldline crosses H. The worldline z(t) := x^{-1}(c t, 0, 0, 0) of the inertial frame satisfies z(0) = x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), which lies on H, and is defined and future timelike for every real t; thus a single regular worldline passes through H from the region x^1 > x^0 (for t < 0 it has x^1 = 0 > x^0 = c t) to the region x^1 < x^0 (for t > 0), which refutes (i) in a second way and contradicts the reading of H as a boundary on which the model fails. What remains true is exactly the conditional statement of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (ii), that the specific congruence worldlines cannot be reached from events with V >= 0; this is a restriction of causal reachability of those worldlines and not a boundary or singularity of the affine model. (e) Scope. All assertions are mathematical statements about the affine model and its causal reachability relations; no physical interpretation, measurement or empirical claim is made, and no choice principle is used.

before.title: Rindler radar distance between two coaxial observers is not symmetric under interchange
before.statement: Statement refuted: 'For every pair of future timelike worldlines y and y' of the model for which the radar protocol of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol applies with y as observer and y' as reflector, the radar distance assigned by y to the reflection event on y' equals the radar distance assigned by y' to the reflection event on y; that is, the radar distance between two observers is symmetric under interchange of observer and reflector.' Counterexample in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar with y = O the worldline rho = rho_0 and y' = R the worldline rho = 2rho_0 (coaxial, with the same y = z = 0 coordinates), rho_0 > 0, c > 0. (a) Radar distance from O to R. Emit from O at the Rindler time theta_e = 0, i.e. from e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0). By pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) the reflection event on R is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) at Rindler time log 2 and the reception event on O is e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2; the round trip takes 2rho_0 log 2/c of O's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by O is D_1 := rho_0 log 2. (b) Radar distance from R to O. Emit from R at theta = 0, i.e. from r_- = x^{-1}(0, 2rho_0, 0, 0). The future null line from r_- towards O is the constant-U line with U = 2rho_0; it meets rho = rho_0 at the Rindler time log 2, at the reflection event q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0), and the return line reaches R at the Rindler time 2 log 2, at the event x^{-1}(15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The round trip takes 4rho_0 log 2/c of R's proper time, so the radar distance assigned by R is D_2 := 2rho_0 log 2. (c) Hence D_2/D_1 = 2 = rho_m/rho_0: the two radar distances between the same pair of worldlines differ, and the assignment is not symmetric. Both assignments are finite and both reflection events lie in the causal future of their respective emission events; the asymmetry is a property of the radar assignment with the two different observers, not a physical anisotropy. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors; the symmetric half-split convention of def-sr-operational-radar-protocol is retained, and no measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made.
before.strategy: Recompute the radar protocol of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the roles of the two worldlines interchanged. (a) is the computation of ex-sr-rindler-radar-distance-worked (a). (b) The future null line from r_- towards smaller rho is the constant-U line U = 2rho_0, i.e. rho = 2rho_0 e^{-theta}; it meets rho = rho_0 at theta = log 2, and the chart coordinates there are (rho_0 sinh(log 2), rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/4, 5rho_0/4, 0, 0) by sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). The return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = 2rho_0 at theta = 2log 2, with coordinates (2rho_0 sinh(2log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/4, 17rho_0/4, 0, 0). The proper-time conversion factor on the worldline rho = const is rho/c per unit Rindler time by pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (i), giving the round-trip proper times 2rho_0 log 2/c and 4rho_0 log 2/c respectively and the radar distances D_1 = rho_0 log 2 and D_2 = 2rho_0 log 2. (c) is the quotient D_2/D_1 = 2. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Worked low-speed correspondence at $|w|=c/5$
before.design_state: exact radical computations with rounded decimals and a check of every displayed bound
before.physical_scope: Numerical specialisation of pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence for a single massive particle state with |w|=c/5 in a named inertial frame of the flat model, in SI conventions. The displayed decimals are rounded values of exact radical expressions, not measurements; no experimental value, uncertainty or precision claim is made, and no other state or frame is covered.
before.statement:
Specialise [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] to one massive particle of mass $m>0$ whose coordinate velocity $w$ in a named inertial frame satisfies $|w|/c=1/5$, so that $z=1/25$ and $z_0=z$. Then $\gamma_w=(1-1/25)^{-1/2}=5/\sqrt{24}=5\sqrt6/12\approx1.0206207262$ and $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(25/24)^{5/2}\approx0.4152916366$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]); all decimals below are rounded and all inequalities are between the exact expressions.

(a) [Rate of the expansion at $z=1/25$] $\gamma_w-1-\tfrac z2=5\sqrt6/12-51/50\approx0.0006207262$, while the bound of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]] is $K(z_0)z^2=\tfrac38(25/24)^{5/2}/625\approx0.0006644666$, so the remainder bound holds and is sharp to about $7\%$ here.

(b) [Energy and kinetic energy] $E_n(P)-mc^2=mc^2(5\sqrt6/12-1)\approx0.0206207262\,mc^2$ while $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac1{50}mc^2=0.02\,mc^2$; the deviation $\approx0.0006207262\,mc^2$ obeys the bound $K(z_0)z\,m|w|^2=mc^2K(z_0)z^2\approx0.0006644666\,mc^2$ (all in units of $mc^2$).

(c) [Momentum] $|q_n(P)|=m\gamma_w|w|=\tfrac{\sqrt6}{12}mc\approx0.2041241452\,mc$ while $|N_p(m,w)|=mc/5=0.2\,mc$; the deviation is $\approx0.0041241452\,mc$ against the bound $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)z\,mc/5=(0.5+0.0166116655)\cdot0.04\,mc/5\approx0.0041328933\,mc$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $|w-q_n(P)/m|/|w|=1-1/\gamma_w=1-2\sqrt6/5\approx0.0202041029$, within the bound $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)z\approx0.0206644666$ of clause (d) of the theorem.

The state is admissible: $z=1/25<1$, and $w$ of norm $c/5$ is realized in a frame chart by the hypothesis; the case $|w|=c$ is not considered, and the numbers carry no empirical content.
before.strategy: (a) Substitution of $z=1/25$ in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]\,(b), with the exact value $\gamma_w=(24/25)^{-1/2}=(25/24)^{1/2}=5/\sqrt6\cdot\ldots$ computed through [[lem-rational-power-laws]] ($(a/b)^{1/2}=a^{1/2}b^{-1/2}$); the displayed decimals are rounded to ten significant digits. (b) and (c) substitute $|w|=c/5$ and $\gamma_w=5\sqrt6/12$ into clauses (a)-(c) of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]], whose premises (the adopted postulate and the frame data) hold by hypothesis; the comparison quantities are $N_K=mc^2/50$ and $|N_p|=mc/5$ from [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. (d) Uses $w-q_n(P)/m=w(1-1/\gamma_w)$ from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) and the bound of the theorem's clause (d). The inequality checks are arithmetic comparisons of the displayed exact expressions; the rounded decimals are computational illustrations only.
