before.title: Rindler radar distances worked: reflectors at twice and at half the observer's radius
before.statement: Worked computation in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar. Let c > 0, fix rho_0 > 0 and take y_0 = z_0 = 0; let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0 with Rindler time theta = c tau/rho_0, and take the emission event e_- at theta_e = 0, so that e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0) in the inertial chart x. (a) Reflector at rho_m = 2rho_0. The future null line from e_- of constant V has V = -rho_0, and it meets rho = 2rho_0 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws) the reflection event is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0), and the return event is e_+ = x^{-1}(rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time theta(e_+) = 2 log 2. Thus (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = log 2 = theta_m, the radar time assigned to q_m is (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant of O's proper time, and the radar distance is rho_0 log 2. The two worldlines rho = rho_0 and rho = 2rho_0 are at rest distance rho_0 in the slice theta = log 2; since e > 2 gives log 2 < 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance. (b) Reflector at rho_m = rho_0/2. The future null line from e_- of constant U has U = rho_0, and it meets rho = rho_0/2 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 the reflection event is q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0) and the return event is again e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2. The radar time is again (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant and the radar distance is again rho_0 log 2, while the rest distance in the slice theta = log 2 is now rho_0/2; since e < 3 < 4 gives log 2 > 1/2 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is now strictly larger than the rest distance. (c) The two cases show that the radar distance rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)| to a coaxial reflector is not a function of the rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|: the same radar distance rho_0 log 2 is assigned to reflectors whose rest distances are rho_0 and rho_0/2. In both cases the midpoint property theta_m = (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) is verified exactly, and the round-trip proper time of O is 2rho_0 log 2/c. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors in the flat classical model; no measurement, apparatus, source or statistical claim, and no empirical inference, is made, and the idealizations of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (v) are retained.
before.strategy: Substitute the two reflector radii into the exact radar computation of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii). (a) With theta_e = 0 the constant-V line through e_- carries V = -rho_0; meeting rho = 2rho_0 gives -2rho_0 e^{-theta} = -rho_0, i.e. e^{-theta} = 1/2 and theta_m = log 2; the chart coordinates of q_m are (2rho_0 sinh(log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) by the exact values sinh(log 2) = 3/4, cosh(log 2) = 5/4, which follow from the defining exponentials. The return line is the constant-U line through q_m and meets rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = 2log 2, giving e_+ = (rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) (sinh(2log 2) = 15/8, cosh(2log 2) = 17/8). The radar time and distance follow from the protocol formula of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the round-trip proper time rho_0(2log 2)/c of O; the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The inequality log 2 < 1 is the strict increase of log and 2 < e (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (b) With theta_e = 0 the constant-U line through e_- carries U = rho_0; meeting rho = rho_0/2 gives (rho_0/2) e^{theta} = rho_0, i.e. theta_m = log 2, and the reflection event is ((rho_0/2) sinh(log 2), (rho_0/2) cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0); the return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = rho_0 again at theta = 2log 2, giving the same return event as in (a). The radar quantities are as displayed, and log 2 > 1/2 follows from 4 > e and strict increase of log (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (c) The two computations differ only in the rest distance while the radar distance is the same; this is the comparison clause used in the statement. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Rindler radar distances worked: reflectors at twice and at half the observer's radius
after.statement: Worked computation in the Rindler chart of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar. Let c > 0, fix rho_0 > 0 and take y_0 = z_0 = 0; let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0 with Rindler time theta = c tau/rho_0, and take the emission event e_- at theta_e = 0, so that e_- = x^{-1}(0, rho_0, 0, 0) in the inertial chart x. (a) Reflector at rho_m = 2rho_0. The future null line from e_- of constant V has V = -rho_0, and it meets rho = 2rho_0 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives, thm-natural-logarithm-laws) the reflection event is q_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0), and the return event is e_+ = x^{-1}(rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time theta(e_+) = 2 log 2. Thus (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = log 2 = theta_m, the radar time assigned to q_m is (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant of O's proper time, and the radar distance is rho_0 log 2. The two worldlines rho = rho_0 and rho = 2rho_0 are at rest distance rho_0 in the slice theta = log 2; since e > 2 gives log 2 < 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is strictly smaller than the rest distance. (b) Reflector at rho_m = rho_0/2. The future null line from e_- of constant U has U = rho_0, and it meets rho = rho_0/2 at the Rindler time theta_m = log 2; using sinh(log 2) = 3/4 and cosh(log 2) = 5/4 the reflection event is q'_m = x^{-1}(3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0) and the return event is again e_+ = x^{-1}(15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) at Rindler time 2 log 2. The radar time is again (rho_0/c) log 2 plus the base constant and the radar distance is again rho_0 log 2, while the rest distance in the slice theta = log 2 is now rho_0/2; since e < 3 < 4 gives log 2 > 1/2 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws), the radar distance is now strictly larger than the rest distance. (c) The two cases (a)-(b) give the same radar distance $\rho_0\log2$ at distinct rest distances $\rho_0$ and $\rho_0/2$; this demonstrates noninjectivity of the assignment as the reflector radius varies. To prove that radar distance is not determined by the rest distance alone, also take $\rho_m=3\rho_0/2$. With the same emission at $\theta_e=0$, the reflection occurs at $\theta_m=\log(3/2)$, at $q''_m=x^{-1}(5\rho_0/8,13\rho_0/8,0,0)$, and the return occurs at $2\log(3/2)$, at $e''_+=x^{-1}(65\rho_0/72,97\rho_0/72,0,0)$. This reflector has rest distance $\rho_0/2$, equal to case (b), but radar distance $\rho_0\log(3/2)<\rho_0\log2$, because $3/2<2$ and log is strictly increasing. These equal inputs and unequal outputs prove the stated failure of dependence on rest distance alone. The original two cases both satisfy $\theta_m=(\theta_e+\theta(e_+))/2$ and have round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log2/c$; the third case satisfies the same midpoint identity and has round-trip proper time $2\rho_0\log(3/2)/c$. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors in the flat classical model; no measurement, apparatus, source or statistical claim, and no empirical inference, is made, and the idealizations of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (v) are retained.
after.strategy: Substitute the two reflector radii into the exact radar computation of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii). (a) With theta_e = 0 the constant-V line through e_- carries V = -rho_0; meeting rho = 2rho_0 gives -2rho_0 e^{-theta} = -rho_0, i.e. e^{-theta} = 1/2 and theta_m = log 2; the chart coordinates of q_m are (2rho_0 sinh(log 2), 2rho_0 cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/2, 5rho_0/2, 0, 0) by the exact values sinh(log 2) = 3/4, cosh(log 2) = 5/4, which follow from the defining exponentials. The return line is the constant-U line through q_m and meets rho = rho_0 at theta(e_+) = 2log 2, giving e_+ = (rho_0 sinh(2log 2), rho_0 cosh(2log 2), 0, 0) = (15rho_0/8, 17rho_0/8, 0, 0) (sinh(2log 2) = 15/8, cosh(2log 2) = 17/8). The radar time and distance follow from the protocol formula of pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar (iii) with the round-trip proper time rho_0(2log 2)/c of O; the rest distance uses the slice metric drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The inequality log 2 < 1 is the strict increase of log and 2 < e (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (b) With theta_e = 0 the constant-U line through e_- carries U = rho_0; meeting rho = rho_0/2 gives (rho_0/2) e^{theta} = rho_0, i.e. theta_m = log 2, and the reflection event is ((rho_0/2) sinh(log 2), (rho_0/2) cosh(log 2), 0, 0) = (3rho_0/8, 5rho_0/8, 0, 0); the return line is the constant-V line through q'_m and meets rho = rho_0 again at theta = 2log 2, giving the same return event as in (a). The radar quantities are as displayed, and log 2 > 1/2 follows from log4=2log2>log e=1, since 4 > e and log is strictly increasing (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws). (c) Cases (a)-(b) alone prove that distinct reflector radii and rest distances can give the same radar distance; they do not establish failure of dependence on rest distance alone. For the additional radius 3rho_0/2, constant V=-rho_0 gives theta_m=log(3/2). The defining exponentials give sinh(log(3/2))=5/12 and cosh(log(3/2))=13/12; multiplying by 3rho_0/2 gives (5rho_0/8,13rho_0/8). The return has theta=2log(3/2), for which e^theta=9/4 and e^(-theta)=4/9, hence sinh theta=65/72 and cosh theta=97/72; multiplying by rho_0 gives the stated return coordinates. The outgoing displacement from (0,rho_0) is (5rho_0/8,5rho_0/8), future null. The return displacement from q''_m is (5rho_0/18,-5rho_0/18), future null. The third reflector and the radius rho_0/2 reflector both have rest distance rho_0/2, while their radar distances are rho_0 log(3/2) and rho_0 log2, unequal by strict increase of log. This completes the full claim with all earlier examples and midpoint calculations preserved. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Local conservation of stress-energy for the adopted matter models
before.statement: Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. (b) If $\rho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $\rho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (d) For a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field prescribed on $\Omega$ that is not obtained from one of the adopted models together with its field equations, no conservation is asserted; a conservation statement about such a field is an additional explicit premise. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate.
before.strategy: Clause (a) is [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solutions of the adopted field equation; clause (b) is [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]; clause (c) is [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]. Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusion carries no measurement interpretation.

(b) If $ho>0$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted dust equations, then $T=ho\,n\otimes n$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely if $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ and $ho>0$ then the dust equations hold. (c) If $\varepsilon,P$ and the future unit field $n$ satisfy the adopted fluid equations, then $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$ satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$; conversely conservation of that $T$ implies the two fluid equations. (e) The theorem is a conditional deduction from the adopted model equations; it asserts no interaction, force law, cross section, measurement or empirical fact, and its conclusions inherit the scope of the postulate. Under the already stated homogeneous dust reading, the tensor boost computation has the conditional physical interpretation $T'^{00}=\gamma^2ho$. For comoving identical massive particles with fixed rest mass $m$, rest number density $
u$ and $ho=
u mc^2$, a rest rectangular parcel has boosted simultaneous volume $1/\gamma$ times its rest volume (the parallel length contracts and transverse lengths are unchanged), so its particle density is $\gamma
u$; the adopted massive-particle reading gives each particle energy $\gamma mc^2$. Thus the two factors in $\gamma^2ho$ correspond respectively to particle energy and volume/density. This is conditional model interpretation for that homogeneous particle realization, not a derivation of the continuum from microscopic dynamics, a claim about arbitrary tensors, or empirical evidence.

Clause (d) records the absence of any derivation for arbitrary prescribed tensors: the local balance $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$ of [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]] is a definition, and no hypothesis in this page forces $f=0$ for an arbitrary $T$. Clause (e) restates the physical scope. No empirical premise is used and the conclusions inherit only the adopted ideal model readings, with no reported measurement or empirical support. For the preserved dust energy/volume explanation, use the massive-particle energy formula of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] and the parallel/transverse length formulas of [[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] on the stipulated homogeneous rest rectangular parcel. Divide its same particle count by the contracted simultaneous volume and multiply by the particle energy. The exact tensor computation itself is $T'^{00}=\rho(\Lambda^0{}_0)^2=\gamma^2\rho$ from [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](iii). This physical explanation is restricted to the explicitly interpreted homogeneous dust and introduces no interaction, statistical or measured claim.

before.title: Limits of the Newtonian bridge: speed-dependent error constants, the excluded massless case, and bounded chart regions
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("rem failure at relativistic/null speeds"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row ("not a universal cross-framework identification")
before.design_state: scope remark recording the three failure modes as consequences of the cited displayed identities
before.physical_scope: Scope remark for the flat special-relativity massive-particle model and the same bounded low-speed domain as pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence: it records the failure of any speed-independent error constant as |w| -> c, the exclusion of ideal massless particles, and the bounded-region restriction of the Galilean chart limit. It asserts no new physical law, no dynamics, and no empirical statement.
before.statement:
Scope remark on the limits of the low-speed bridge. Each quantitative assertion is an immediate consequence of the cited displayed identities; none of them is used as a premise elsewhere on this page.

(i) [No speed-independent error constant] Let $m>0$. For every $B\ge0$ there are a future unit $n\in V$, a vector $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and a state $P=mU$ whose relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) satisfies $|w|<c$ and $\bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\bigr|>B$, with $T_n$ as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Explicitly, for every integer $\gamma\ge2$ there is such a state with Lorentz factor $\gamma$, namely $|w|=c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$, for which [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ while $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, so $$T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2=mc^2\Bigl(\gamma-\tfrac32+\tfrac{1}{2\gamma^2}\Bigr)\to\infty\quad(\gamma\to\infty),$$ and the relative deviation from the Newtonian value equals $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}\to\infty$. Consequently the constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] necessarily depend on the speed bound $z_0$, no bound of that form is uniform on the whole domain $|w|<c$, and $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$ are unbounded as $|w|\to c$ although $\tfrac12m|w|^2\le\tfrac12mc^2$ there.

(ii) [The massless case is excluded, not a limit] An ideal massless particle of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] carries a nonzero future null four-momentum $P$ and, by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), satisfies $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$ exactly; it has no four-velocity, proper time or relative velocity, and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned to it. The hypotheses $m>0$ and $z\le z_0<1$ exclude it, and no substitution $w$ with $|w|=c$ is available because $\gamma_w$ is undefined there. The bridge therefore concerns massive particles only, and it neither derives nor constrains the ideal massless case or light.

(iii) [Bounded chart regions, not a limit of frameworks] The uniform chart statement [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]] holds on each bounded region $D_{T,R}$ and fails on unbounded regions (its clause (d)); the correspondence is a conditional statement about the adopted model in a bounded low-speed domain, and it is neither an equivalence between the relativistic and Newtonian frameworks, nor a physical process in which the constant $c$ varies, nor empirical evidence for either framework. The Newtonian comparison quantities [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]] are comparison expressions, not the derived quantities of a separate theory.
before.strategy: A scope remark whose clauses are the displayed consequences of earlier items, recorded without proof obligations. (i) For each integer $\gamma\ge2$ one has $\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}<1$; taking $w$ of that rescaled norm in $n^\perp$ and $U=\gamma(n+w/c)$ gives $\eta(U,U)=-1$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) supplies $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$; the displayed difference and its ratio $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}$ are elementary algebra in $\mathbb R$ ([[def-rational-power]] conventions for the exponents). Since $\gamma$ is arbitrary, no real $B$ bounds the difference uniformly, which is exactly the claim that the constant of the correspondence must depend on $z_0$. (ii) Repeats the defining exclusions of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] and the null identity of the batch-8 lemma; there is no new claim. (iii) Repeats the bounded-region clause (d) of the chart lemma and the scope clause (e) of the correspondence theorem.

Since $\gamma$ is arbitrary, no real $B$ bounds the difference uniformly, which is exactly the claim that the constant of the correspondence must depend on $z_0$. (ii) Repeats the defining exclusions of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] and the null identity of the batch-8 lemma; there is no new claim. (iii) Repeats the bounded-region clause (d) of the chart lemma and the scope clause (e) of the correspondence theorem. Fix n and a unit e in its rest space once, and take w=c sqrt(1−gamma^−2)e. Then −eta(U/c,n)=gamma exactly. For any B>=0, thm-of-archimedean supplies an integer gamma>max(2,B/(mc²)+3/2); the displayed difference is greater than mc²(gamma−3/2)>B. The relative ratio exceeds gamma−1 and is unbounded by the same Archimedean property. No sequence of independently chosen unit vectors or additional choice premise is needed.

before.title: Integrated four-momentum of an isolated system on finite slices
before.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. Put $Q^b(s):=\int_{\bar K}T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ and $P^b:=Q^b/c$. Then: (a) $Q^b(s)$ is finite for every $s\in[s_1,s_2]$ and $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$; (b) consequently $P^b$ is independent of $s\in[s_1,s_2]$; if $P$ is future timelike, its invariant mass $\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$ is independent of $s$ as well; (c) if the side flux does not vanish, the exact balance is the finite-flux identity of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]], and no conservation is asserted; (d) no transformation law for $P^b$ under a change of inertial chart or slicing is asserted: without an admissible-region flux argument, $P^b$ is a chart-component integral and is not claimed to be a four-vector; no noncompact, asymptotic or gravitational-energy statement is made, and the reading of $P^b$ as the system's four-momentum is the model's interpretation of the integral, not a measurement.
before.strategy: Clause (a) applies [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(c) to the box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ under the measured hypotheses (conservation and vanishing side flux); the invariance of the invariant mass in (b) is immediate because $P$ is a constant future timelike vector and $\eta(P,P)$ is then constant, using the invariant-mass formula of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]. Clause (c) is the general balance case of the same theorem. Clause (d) records the exact scope: the theorem proves constancy of the chart integrals and nothing about their transformation under a change of chart, which would require the oriented hypersurface flux construction; no noncompact limit is taken. No empirical premise is used.
